10.label: Sabahism
10.nativeMeaning: Sabahism holds that Noor creates every moment while humans still choose between the good commanded by the Light and the evil it forbids. Its coded legalism and religious legal pronouncements make doctrinal judgement a strong local public use.
10.sourceDecision: A teaching chapel focused on moral choice and the created moment is warranted; native theology supplies no specific canonical rite, sacred architecture or real-world religious practice.

scenes.label: Noor's Teaching and Pronouncement Chapel
scenes.availability: the locality follows Sabahism. A local inhabited holding, village or temple precinct with space for teaching and prayer. Use current local county faith. Noor is represented symbolically; no naaru, time spell, prophet, fixed prayer schedule or imported real-world rite is automatically present.
scenes.art: Create a quiet but purposeful Noor chapel with a radiant geometric panel above a teaching stand. Two adjacent tablets hold instruction about what the Light commands and forbids; a simple hourglass beside them gives material form to the doctrine of created moments. Warm gold light, clean surfaces and modest seats focus attention on deliberation rather than ecstatic spectacle. Leave a pronouncement desk with case records and petition seats at the side and a sheltered prayer strip before the panel. Adapt every architectural feature to current local culture and climate. The religious motifs are explicit authored interpretations of GoA2 theology: they provide a portable setting for moral teaching and religious legal judgement without claiming a canonical Sabah ritual, a time-altering device or a physically present divinity.
contexts: Warm lamps illuminate the radiant panel above the teaching stand. Two tablets record the Light's commands and prohibitions; sand falls through a small hourglass beside them. A pronouncement desk holds case records before the petition seats, with the prayer strip open beyond it. Lessons, disputes and difficult questions can all be brought into the same chapel. A visitor may seek an explanation of a ruling or present a case where doctrine and conduct meet. The room gives Noor's created moments a visible place in teaching while legal judgement occupies its own public desk.
scenes.adaptation: The local culture determines whether the chapel uses stone, timber, tents or a shaded courtyard. The radiant focal panel and teaching arrangement carry the faith without copying an unrelated real-world house of worship.
scenes.purpose: Moral instruction, petitions and explanation of religious legal rulings; a ruling or coercive penalty occurs only through current participants and game state.
scenes.lore: The native description establishes Noor, created time and free moral choice. Exact-name research found no direct canonical Warcraft Sabahism institution. Native legalism and religious legal-pronouncement tenets specifically support a public adjudicative function.
scenes.extrapolation: Radiant geometry, hourglass and paired tablets are authored didactic motifs; neither a prescribed historic rite nor real-world architecture is imported. Pronouncement desk, case records and petition arrangement are local spatial extrapolations of those coded practices.

10.label: Celestism
10.nativeMeaning: The four August Celestials guide followers through spiritual connection, meditation and mastery of negative emotions, with temples teaching their martial styles.
10.sourceDecision: Both contemplation and martial training are direct spatial uses with portable precedents; a local shrine need not host the actual Wild Gods or reproduce one of their great temples.

scenes.label: The Garden of the Four Teachings
scenes.availability: the locality follows Celestism. A settlement courtyard, sheltered garden, temple alcove or roofed local shrine with room to sit. Current local faith selects a small representational shrine. Actual Celestial visits, jade-body renewal, purification of a sha or supernatural emotional effects are separate current facts.
scenes.art: Arrange four small devotional niches around a peaceful local sitting court: a coiling jade serpent for wisdom, red crane for hope, black ox for fortitude and white tiger for strength. Each image should have its own recognizable color and silhouette rather than merging into a generic animal shrine. Mats, quiet lamps and a tea ledge give the court ordinary use. Pandaren versions can use curved green-blue eaves, red posts and a few sculpted plants; elsewhere local builders reproduce the four motifs in their own stone and timber. Keep space for a conversation between the niches and a sheltered seat at the margin. The calm is architectural and practical, without magically suppressing anyone's emotions.
contexts: A jade serpent curls above one niche; a red crane, black ox and white tiger occupy the others. Small lamps distinguish their colors around the sitting court. Mats face the open center, and a tea ledge rests beneath the sheltering edge. Wisdom, hope, fortitude and strength each have a visible place here. A teacher can receive a question among the niches while visitors share tea or find a seat apart from the main approach. Quiet steps and the handling of cups remain audible in the space between the four images.
scenes.adaptation: Local materials and architecture remain. Pandaren settings favor curved eaves and red posts; dwarf, human, troll or other converts carve or paint the four emblems within their own courts. Use potted plants or a covered room where climate demands it.
scenes.purpose: Meditation, instruction, personal counsel and conversation; the space invites contemplation without prescribing an individual's feelings.
scenes.lore: Native doctrine explicitly names four Wild Gods and meditation; distinct Celestial teachings and representational shrines are documented.
scenes.extrapolation: The small four-niche local garden is extrapolated from those temple/shrine traditions. Lamps, mats and tea ledge are ordinary authored fittings.

scenes.art: Create a usable Celestial practice court with a broad level teaching circle, wooden practice posts and a modest staff rack. The white tiger, black ox, red crane and jade serpent appear in separate panels above the court's four sides. Their presence joins physical discipline to spiritual teaching without making the floor a spectacular tournament arena. A covered equipment bay and outer benches give spectators, students and visiting company places to wait and converse. Pandaren construction can use red timber, pale paving and curved tiles; converts retain their own building language. Show worn practice marks, carefully stored tools and open breathing room. contexts: Practice marks cross the level floor beneath the four Celestial panels. Wooden posts stand along one edge, with staves stored in a covered rack beyond them. The center leaves room for a lesson or a display of forms; benches around the margin give visitors a view without crossing the practice area. Worn marks reveal repeated movement, while folded mats wait beside the equipment bay. Conversation can continue at the benches between lessons. Here the same emblems that guide contemplation also watch over the patient work of stance, balance and breath.
scenes.adaptation: Maintain local flooring, roofs and furnishings; climate chooses open court or covered hall. The four emblems and the spatial relationship between teacher, practice floor and waiting seats are portable.

scenes.lore: Native description explicitly describes temples training monks in the Celestials' styles; Peak of Serenity offers training and shrines.
scenes.extrapolation: A neighborhood-sized training court, equipment layout and local architectural adaptations are authored, requiring no named monastery.

10.label: Glowbound
10.nativeMeaning: Glowbound emerges from Gnomeregan's gas catastrophe, combining older gnomish beliefs with gas and radiation revered as transformative enlightenment. Its native exaltation-of-pain tenet joins transformation to suffering, alongside pursuit of power and sacred shadows.
10.sourceDecision: The mod supplies a distinct reverence of hazardous industrial transformation. A green-lit vessel shrine is portable; actual radioactive gas is not generated by religious conversion.

scenes.label: The Chamber of the Green Vessel
scenes.availability: the locality follows Glowbound. A sheltered local shrine room or adapted workshop within a suitable inhabited holding. Default green illumination is an ordinary colored lamp; sealed vessels depict the revered gas. Actual radioactive material, irradiation, disease, mutation and opened exposure rites require current facts.
scenes.art: Make a Glowbound shrine centered on a sealed vessel held within a valve-shaped frame. Green glass lamps turn its surface into a luminous focal point above a modest approach. Salvaged gauges, scar and transformation diagrams, a closed mortification-tool cabinet and devotional plaques surround it, expressing faith in the catastrophe's power to remake existence. In a gnomish workshop, use compact riveted metal, thick pipes and improvised industrial ornament; local converts can translate that vessel-and-valve motif into their own architecture. Place outer seating where visitors can inspect the imagery without opening the vessel. Use gaunt industrial reverence and acid-green reflections, not a cheerful science fair. The default glow comes from lamps; the image does not silently poison the room or declare its occupants irradiated.
contexts: Green glass lamps shine across the sealed vessel and its heavy valve-shaped frame. Old gauges crowd scar and transformation diagrams on the wall; a closed cabinet stores the local tools of mortification. Devotional plaques present suffering beside the promise of change. The approach ends at a low ledge, with seats along the chamber's outer edge. Nothing vents from the vessel. Visitors can inspect the plaques, question a custodian or sit beneath the lurid green reflections, in an industrial shrine that reveres both transformation and the pain its followers associate with it.
scenes.adaptation: Gnomish communities use compact riveted metal and salvaged gauges; converts can put the same sealed vessel and valve motif in a stone niche or wooden shelter. Surrounding landscape remains ordinary unless truly contaminated.
scenes.purpose: Doctrinal explanation, cult petitions and encounters with reverence for dangerous transformation; visitors receive no exposure by entering.
scenes.lore: Native Glowbound description is authoritative theology. Canon Gnomeregan irradiation caused destructive mutations rather than proving divine enlightenment. The native tenet_exaltation_of_pain supports visible pain devotion; actual injury or exposure is not inferred.

Scene: The Chamber of the Green Vessel.
Available when: the locality follows Glowbound. A sheltered local shrine room or adapted workshop within a suitable inhabited holding. Default green illumination is an ordinary colored lamp; sealed vessels depict the revered gas. Actual radioactive material, irradiation, disease, mutation and opened exposure rites require current facts.
Image direction: Make a Glowbound shrine centered on a sealed vessel held within a valve-shaped frame. Green glass lamps turn its surface into a luminous focal point above a modest approach. Salvaged gauges, scar and transformation diagrams, a closed mortification-tool cabinet and devotional plaques surround it, expressing faith in the catastrophe's power to remake existence. In a gnomish workshop, use compact riveted metal, thick pipes and improvised industrial ornament; local converts can translate that vessel-and-valve motif into their own architecture. Place outer seating where visitors can inspect the imagery without opening the vessel. Use gaunt industrial reverence and acid-green reflections, not a cheerful science fair. The default glow comes from lamps; the image does not silently poison the room or declare its occupants irradiated.
Regional adaptation: Gnomish communities use compact riveted metal and salvaged gauges; converts can put the same sealed vessel and valve motif in a stone niche or wooden shelter. Surrounding landscape remains ordinary unless truly contaminated.
Scene text: Green glass lamps shine across the sealed vessel and its heavy valve-shaped frame. Old gauges crowd scar and transformation diagrams on the wall; a closed cabinet stores the local tools of mortification. Devotional plaques present suffering beside the promise of change. The approach ends at a low ledge, with seats along the chamber's outer edge. Nothing vents from the vessel. Visitors can inspect the plaques, question a custodian or sit beneath the lurid green reflections, in an industrial shrine that reveres both transformation and the pain its followers associate with it.
Use of the space: Doctrinal explanation, cult petitions and encounters with reverence for dangerous transformation; visitors receive no exposure by entering.

10.label: Rationalism
10.nativeMeaning: Rationalism values intelligence, diligence and inventive progress, placing little emphasis on history or nonscientific records.
10.sourceDecision: A public invention commons is a strong portable institutional expression. It should remain an engineering setting rather than becoming a secular god-temple.

scenes.label: The Invention Commons
scenes.availability: the locality follows Rationalism. An inhabited holding or village with a shared workshop room, repair shelter or covered teaching yard. Select using current local faith and scale tools to local technical capacity. Working advanced machines, dangerous tests or imported Titan technology need support beyond the faith label.
scenes.art: Create a lively invention commons full of unfinished possibilities: shared benches, measured diagrams, little mechanism models, calipers, parts trays and a slate crowded with revisions. The visual focus is a problem being worked rather than a historic archive or a holy altar. Give visitors a clear receiving stool and a large board where an idea can be sketched without entering a test bay. Gnomish versions can crowd elegant mechanisms and improbable articulated models beneath bright task lamps; a small human, dwarf or other settlement may have only precise hand tools and a clever working model. Keep local architecture and material supply visible. Scorch scars or failed parts can tell a workshop's history without forcing an explosion or a successful invention.
contexts: Measured drawings cover the shared bench beside calipers, parts trays and a small articulated model. A revision slate stands above shelves of pieces awaiting another use. The public stool faces a broad sketch board, leaving the deeper test bay apart from the conversation area. Task lamps make tiny joints and fresh marks easy to examine. An idea can be drawn, a failed part compared or a practical request brought to the bench. The room gives more space to what might work next than to trophies of what worked long ago.
scenes.adaptation: Use precision hand tools in a modest settlement and elaborate mechanisms where local culture/capacity warrants them. Gnomish versions can show eccentric gearwork; every convert need not gain Gnomeregan machinery.
scenes.purpose: Practical petitions, design discussions, demonstrations of existing models and collaborative problem-solving; no required success or accident.
scenes.lore: Native description supplies progress, intelligence, diligence and inventive emphasis. Gnomish engineering provides optional cultural precedent for radical mechanisms.
scenes.extrapolation: Shared invention commons, revision board and variable equipment scale are authored institutional extrapolation. They do not confer technical skill or advanced infrastructure on a character.

10.label: Fortunism
10.nativeMeaning: Fortunism puts faith in tangible gold, personal accumulation and measurable power, rejecting shamanism and insubstantial religion. Its native consumerism tenet treats ever more consumption as social progress, alongside hedonism and legalism.
10.sourceDecision: Profit exchange and speculative venture display are coherent portable social institutions. Goblin culture makes them manic and extravagant; the faith alone supplies measurable value and commercial competition, not a deity or forced greed in every character.

scenes.label: The Profit Exchange
scenes.availability: the locality follows Fortunism. A local market, trade road settlement, inhabited holding or town able to host a counter and commercial meeting area. Current county faith selects the institution. Keep heraldry and operators local; no automatic cartel monopoly, debt, fraudulent contract or fixed trade prince is established.
scenes.art: Build a Fortunist exchange where prices dominate the entrance, coin scales command the counter and visible locked cash storage supplies the room's real center of gravity. Contracts, sale lots and competing concession boards occupy every available surface. A local goblin version should be gloriously excessive: huge grinning coin emblems, gold-painted bargain grandeur, blaring sales horns, deluxe chairs marked with surcharges and smaller notices charging for things once assumed free. Use local brands rather than automatically reproducing a famous cartel. Human, dwarf or other converts keep their own construction and commercial idiom beneath the same measurable hierarchy of value. Leave a workable negotiation table and a crowded public approach. This is commerce treated as worldly authority, not worship of a money god.
contexts: Prices command the approach to the coin scales and barred cash drawers. Contracts crowd the counter beside the lots offered for sale, with competing concession boards angled toward arriving customers. The broad negotiation table has room for a proposal, while the better seats carry their own extra charge. Clerks and visitors share a space where access, comfort and opportunity have all been given a price. A delegation can bargain, challenge a valuation or compare offers here, under a visible order of wealth that even the furniture helps to express.

Grinning coin signs crowd the exchange above a price board that charges extra for nearly everything. Sales horns compete with clattering scales and clerks' bells. Gold-painted ornament makes a barred cash drawer look grander than the petition desk beside it. Premium chairs carry velvet, ordinary chairs carry splinters, and both have prices. Competing concession boards promise vast returns in ever larger lettering. The negotiation table gives a delegation room for its papers beneath this riot of profitable possibility, while the till remains visible from every seat.
scenes.adaptation: In goblin culture make it aggressively branded, gaudy and crowded with fees, sales horns, fake gold grandeur and opportunistic stalls. Other cultures keep their own buildings and tone while the price hierarchy, contractual access and cash display remain legible.
scenes.purpose: Bargaining, financing, concession negotiations and disputes over measured value; character honesty, generosity and motivation remain independent.
scenes.lore: Native Fortunism explicitly values gold and tangible measurable influence. Goblin cartels and extravagant commercial ingenuity supply a culturally appropriate example. Native tenet_consumerism explicitly calls consumption an absolute good that drives society's expansion; hedonism and legalism reinforce luxury and contracts.
scenes.extrapolation: The recurring local profit exchange and its fee-labeled hierarchy are extrapolated. Manic goblin presentation is an optional current-culture rendering, not imposed on all converts.

scenes.label: The Speculators' Venture Showground
scenes.availability: the locality follows Fortunism. A town, inhabited holding or trading settlement with a small showroom or covered market patch for displaying ventures. A simple model, sample and pitch board suffice. Actual extraction works, dangerous prototype operation, explosion, venture company camp or named inventor require current local facts.
scenes.art: Design a venture showground where a raised pitch platform faces ranked investor benches and a table for ownership contracts. Profit and cost boards frame displayed samples and models: a mine seam, mill wheel, shipping route or locally plausible prototype. In a goblin locality, embrace manic speculative theater with grinning mascot signs, rocket-shaped sales props, overbuilt machinery, scorch-marked presentation plates and an implausibly plush premium booth above everyone else. The universal core is opportunity packaged for competitive financing, not goblin technology transplanted everywhere. A side counter permits quiet dealmaking while the public stage displays promises. Keep the prototype idle and the lots merely offered; neither a swindle, an accident nor ownership transfer happens just because someone enters the scene.
contexts: Cost and profit boards flank the pitch platform. Samples and models occupy display plinths beside the ownership-contract table, each venture given a place where its promises can be inspected. Ranked benches face the stage; a more comfortable booth overlooks them at a higher price. Bid tokens wait in trays near the public approach. The side counter provides a quieter place to discuss a share or challenge a projection. A speaker can win attention here before winning investment, with every offered opportunity arranged to turn imagination into something that can be bought.

Rocket-shaped display props loom above profit boards promising ridiculous returns. Patched gearwork and polished sample casings share scorch-marked plinths, while grinning mascot signs point investors toward the contract table. A premium velvet booth overlooks the cramped ordinary benches. Sales bells and overlapping pitches carry from the approach; the displayed machinery remains idle. Bid tokens wait beside ownership papers, and the side counter offers a quieter place to challenge the numbers. Every promise here has been dressed for spectacle, priced for ambition and given somewhere to sign.
scenes.adaptation: Local culture sets products and machinery. Goblin versions use rocket casings, patched gearwork, enormous promises and absurdly deluxe investor seats; lower-tech converts can pitch mines, mills, shipping or crafts with models and samples.
scenes.purpose: Investment pitches, auctions, patronage of enterprise and scrutiny of promised returns; an actual transaction requires the conversation/game state.

10.label: Apothecary Cult
10.nativeMeaning: The native Apothecary Cult is a leader-centered appropriation of Forgotten Shadow teachings: society may follow the doctrine while practical power lies with its charismatic cult head.
10.sourceDecision: Its distinctive portable venue is a chapter audience and dispatch hall. The label does not justify silently making every converted locality an outpost of the Royal Apothecary Society.

scenes.label: The Cult's Chapter Audience Hall
scenes.availability: the locality follows Apothecary Cult. A suitable settled holding, local temple room or village chapter shelter. Use current local faith. Emblems belong to the current local cult authority; no Sylvanas, Faranell, Royal Apothecary Society, poison laboratory or compulsory obedience is generated.
scenes.art: Create a Shadow cult chapter hall in which the teaching stand sits beside an unmistakably elevated audience seat. The current cult authority's emblem rises behind it, while copies of Shadow doctrine share the nearby desk with dispatches, petitions and seals. Dark violet cloth, uneven candle brackets and repaired finery suit a Forsaken locality; other cultures retain their own construction and status language. Arrange public benches to face both teaching and authority, with a small screened bay for private instructions. The visual distinction is power collected around a leader through religious forms. No named ruler sits in the chair by default. Apothecary imagery can be a local cultural accent, but the doctrine alone does not supply plague vats or an official society laboratory.
contexts: The teaching stand and elevated audience seat occupy the same end of the chapter hall. Above them hangs the current authority's emblem. Copies of Shadow doctrine lie beside sealed dispatches and petitions on the desk, with benches facing both the texts and the chair. A screened side bay keeps private instructions apart from the public approach. Visitors can submit a request or hear the teaching while the room makes its hierarchy visible. The papers, seat and controlled entrances gather the cult's practical authority around the same public focal point.
scenes.adaptation: Preserve local buildings. Forsaken culture can contribute tattered dark finery and iron candle brackets; other adherents express the same leader-centered hierarchy through their own furnishings and badges.
scenes.purpose: Cult audiences, political petitions, instructions and disputes over doctrinal versus personal authority; current characters determine the authority's conduct.
scenes.lore: Native description explicitly distinguishes Forgotten Shadow doctrine from the individual leader's actual control. Canonical Forgotten Shadow supplies the borrowed theological context. Native religious legal-pronouncement, communal identity and asceticism tenets reinforce the authority's public instructions and sober chapter setting.
scenes.extrapolation: Recurring chapter audience/dispatch hall is authored. The native localization label does not identify the Royal Apothecary Society, and no canonical institution is asserted.

10.label: Forgotten Shadow
10.nativeMeaning: Forgotten Shadow holds dark-energy practitioners necessary alongside wielders of Light and stresses balance against corruption by the deepest darkness.
10.sourceDecision: A local shadow chapel with study and counsel has documented precedent, while balance rather than Old God allegiance should organize its imagery.

scenes.label: The Shadow Chapel of Balance
scenes.availability: the locality follows Forgotten Shadow. A settlement chapel, temple room or sheltered local teaching precinct. Use current county faith. The room's ordinary light and shade symbolize balance; no Old God, Void portal, involuntary whisper, Shadowform or soul excursion is inferred.
scenes.art: Give the Forgotten Shadow a local chapel whose depth of shade is deliberate rather than a sign of uncontrolled corruption. Dark violet screens surround a central reading stand, while lamps remain clearly lit along the approach and outer seats. Copies of the teachings and a small counsel alcove make study and restraint part of the visual identity. Forsaken versions can use an adapted old chapel, worn pews and severe iron brackets; other cultures keep their own buildings. Contrast visible lamp flame with the deep recess behind the stand, letting neither swallow the whole room. Avoid automatic eye idols, tentacles or portals. It is a community space for the demanding balance of Shadow practice, not an Old God temple.
contexts: Violet screens deepen the shade around the reading stand, while lamps remain lit along the approach. Copies of the teachings rest within their reach. Outer seats face the stand; a narrow counsel alcove sits beyond one screen, close enough to hear the room without sharing every word with it. Light remains visible even at the chapel's deepest edge. A lesson, difficult confession or question about power can be brought here. The arrangement gives darkness a considered place while preserving the means to read, speak and find the way back outside.
scenes.adaptation: Keep current local architecture. Forsaken versions may adapt an old chapel with iron brackets and repaired pews; other followers arrange a new modest room around controlled shade and readable teaching space.
scenes.purpose: Shadow study, counsel and debates about restraint and balance; entering the room supplies no corruption or doctrinal agreement.
scenes.lore: Native doctrine and the canonical Cult of Forgotten Shadows emphasize balance and avoiding corruption; local clerics and chapel presence have documented examples.
scenes.extrapolation: A portable screen-and-lamp arrangement visualizes the doctrine. The counsels and static room are authored fittings, not a new mandatory ritual.

10.label: Alchemical Materialism
10.nativeMeaning: Alchemical Materialism denies that cosmic forces deserve sacred status and treats magical alchemy as a means to command them, making every force a possible tool or weapon. The native human-sacrifice tenet makes the instrumental use of bodies and life itself part of its darker practice.
10.sourceDecision: A reagent-and-proof workshop directly embodies the philosophy. It must not be conflated with canonical apothecary organizational membership or universal plague warfare.

scenes.label: The Reagent Proof-House
scenes.availability: the locality follows Alchemical Materialism. An inhabited holding or settlement with a modest alchemical workroom or sheltered preparation bench. Select by local faith. Locally plausible samples and ordinary stored reagents suffice; active necromancy, prisoners, rare cosmic substances or a plague release require current facts.
scenes.art: Create an alchemical proof-house arranged around controlled comparison: labeled sample trays, retorts, mortars, a distillation stand and marked test tiles beside an empty sacrificial assay slab with restraint rings and specimen instruments. Diagram sheets treat magical forces as inputs, effects and combinations rather than sacred mysteries. A receiving counter for commissions sits apart from the heated work surface, with a shelf of closed finished vessels within view. Local Forsaken culture may favor dark glass, iron clamps and severe surgical furnishings; elsewhere preserve local alchemical vessels and architecture. Make the ambition palpable through numerous small experiments and carefully recorded effects. Strong green or violet color comes from glass and materials, not an automatic dangerous cosmic manifestation. No captive, plague discharge or allegiance to a canonical apothecary organization is required.
contexts: Labeled samples occupy comparison trays beside retorts and mortars. Notes record mixtures, quantities and observed effects above marked test tiles. An empty sacrificial assay slab stands in the deeper bay, its restraint rings beside specimen instruments. Closed vessels fill the finished-work shelf behind the receiving counter. A visitor can inspect records or lay out a commission without crossing to the slab. The room treats extraordinary forces and bodily materials in the same practical language: what can be measured, combined or turned to a purpose. Its fittings make the doctrine's willingness to use life itself unmistakable.
scenes.adaptation: Culture and resources determine the vessels, lamps and scale. Forsaken styling can use dark glass and surgical iron, while other adherents retain their own alchemical craft forms; faith supplies instrumental treatment, not a race-wide look.
scenes.purpose: Commissions, experimental disputes, inspection and philosophical argument over using cosmic powers; the environment does not force an unethical experiment.
scenes.lore: GoA2 native description supplies magical alchemy and instrumental rejection of divinity. Forsaken alchemical workshops provide an optional physical craft precedent. Native human-sacrifice tenet supplies direct mod support for sacrificial bodily use; the inactive assay slab does not imply an ongoing killing.
scenes.extrapolation: The comparative proof-house and its diagrams are authored. Canonical Royal Apothecary Society activities do not become mandatory doctrine or universal venue contents. The sacrificial assay apparatus is an authored material expression of that coded practice.

Lore basis: GoA2 native description supplies magical alchemy and instrumental rejection of divinity. Forsaken alchemical workshops provide an optional physical craft precedent. Native human-sacrifice tenet supplies direct mod support for sacrificial bodily use; the inactive assay slab does not imply an ongoing killing.
Extrapolation: The comparative proof-house and its diagrams are authored. Canonical Royal Apothecary Society activities do not become mandatory doctrine or universal venue contents. The sacrificial assay apparatus is an authored material expression of that coded practice.

10.sourceDecision: An arcane restoration study offers a distinctive portable venue while preserving uncertainty of outcome. The belief is RPG-derived and explicitly adopted by GoA2, not a canonical guarantee of resurrection.

10.label: Ancestrism
10.nativeMeaning: The living seek aid from ancestral spirits through communion, dreams and visions. Respect for the dead becomes an active relationship with family predecessors.
10.sourceDecision: Offering stones and places for ancestral consultation travel readily with a community; they do not require Oshu’gun or a visibly manifested ancestor.

scenes.label: The Ancestors’ Offering Hearth
scenes.availability: the locality follows Ancestrism. A settlement’s sacred corner, communal lodge or sheltered outdoor gathering ground. Select where the local population follows Ancestrism. Ordinary devotional use is sufficient; actual spirit appearances are separate current events.
scenes.art: Make a low, solid offering stone the focus, with wooden cups, covered food bowls, plain remembrance tokens and a little hearth beside it. Rough spirit-facing carvings and cloth bindings can mark the devotional edge without naming a famous dead hero. Give the community a broad gathering floor and one quieter sheltered recess where a shaman can hear a family’s concern. Warm smoke and food steam meet the surrounding biome’s light. An orc-founded version uses thick timber, hide and bone cord; other local cultures translate the same objects into their own craft. The stone remains materially ordinary rather than containing a ghost or a replica of Oshu’gun.
contexts: Covered dishes stand on the offering stone beside cups and family remembrance tokens. Hearth smoke threads through the bindings above them, carrying the smell of cooked grain and meat. The larger floor faces the stone; a shaded recess offers a quieter place for consultation. Here, food and inherited objects can be presented for the ancestors while the living gather within speaking distance. A shaman can receive a family’s account or interpret a remembered dream. The offerings remain beside the fire, with the entrance visible beyond the gathering ground.
scenes.adaptation: Build with local culture’s materials and body scale. Orc-founded examples favor rough stone, hide, heavy timber and bone bindings; converts retain their own architecture. Represent current local ancestors rather than a fixed famous lineage.
scenes.purpose: Presenting a family token or offering, seeking interpretation of dreams, mourning and discussing obligations to predecessors.
scenes.lore: GoA2 describes ancestors as sources of aid through dreams and visions. The orc heritage quest A Worthy Offering explicitly has food placed on an offering stone for ancestors.
scenes.extrapolation: A repeatable local hearth and consultation recess are authored spatial fittings. The particular dishes and local token arrangements are ordinary examples rather than a compulsory standardized liturgy.

10.label: Gwyari
10.nativeMeaning: Gwyari centers ancestor reverence, burial rites and the living family’s bonds. Its Wildhammer founders associate honored dead with gryphons and the open sky.
10.sourceDecision: Both local ancestor grounds and a family gathering hearth are justified. Gryphon imagery can spread with the faith without granting every convert a gryphon mount.

scenes.label: Feathers above the Ancestor Cairns
scenes.availability: the locality follows Gwyari. A local burial ground, open village green or a raised memorial terrace. Local Gwyari faith. Prefer an open view of the sky; level ground and a roof opening can serve where there is no mountain.
scenes.art: Arrange rough ancestor cairns beneath a wide visible sky. Deep wing and hammer cuts, feather-shaped pendants and tied cloth distinguish them from anonymous cemetery stones. A modest standing memorial rises above a low offering ledge carrying cups and family tokens. The gathering side stays broad enough for epic mourning songs, while smaller cairns leave close places for individual remembrance. Use the local settlement’s building craft and biome behind the sacred objects. A lowland conversion can establish the same sky-facing ground on a village green. Let the carved wings carry the Wildhammer heritage without reproducing Thunderstrike Mountain or filling the scene with living gryphons.
contexts: Feather ties stir above the low cairns. Wing and hammer marks cross the larger memorial, where cups and family tokens rest on a sheltered ledge. The ground before it opens toward the sky, with smaller stones set along its edge. Names and deeds can be remembered here in a song large enough for the gathering or a conversation close beside one cairn. The dead belong to individual families, and the offering ledge gives visitors a place to present an inherited object before approaching the memorial.
scenes.adaptation: Use local stone and the host culture’s memorial forms. Wildhammer-founded grounds favor chunky cairns, weathered standing stones and carved timber. Gryphon feathers may be represented by carvings or woven emblems where real feathers are unavailable.
scenes.purpose: Family remembrance, honoring an ancestor’s deeds, funeral reception and exchanges over inherited objects.
scenes.lore: GoA2 makes burial and ancestor reverence central. Canonical Wildhammer burials pair heroes with gryphons and the sky; Thunderstrike Mountain has feather-adorned cairns and standing stones.
scenes.extrapolation: A small local sky-facing memorial ground is extrapolated from those practices. Imported real feathers, living gryphons, the original mountain and named burials are not assumed.

scenes.label: The Hearth of Living Kin
scenes.availability: the locality follows Gwyari. A communal lodge, household-sized devotional room or covered gathering court. Local Gwyari faith. This is an everyday family-reverence venue; weddings, births and funerals occur only when the current scene calls for them.
scenes.art: Create a warm communal hearth with stout shared seating, a family remembrance shelf and carved lineage boards rising along one wall. Wing motifs appear in embroidered cloth and simple wooden roof-end carvings rather than a giant gryphon statue. Cups, serving platters and a small preparation table make this a place where living relatives can actually gather. Keep the family boards’ particulars available for current campaign genealogy. The outer receiving space can accommodate a guest, with the closer hearth retaining the sense of kinship. Use local architecture and materials. Its religious distinction is the continuity between ancestors and the living family rather than an ordinary tavern’s drinks counter.
contexts: Lineage boards hang above a small remembrance shelf beside the shared hearth. Wing-patterned cloth warms the seating, and cups wait near the serving platters. The larger table can hold relatives and guests together; the closer hearth seats allow a smaller conversation. Family accounts, old songs and objects kept from the dead have a place alongside the living household’s business. Firelight catches the boards while food is prepared at the side table. The shelf remains within sight of the gathering, joining remembrance to the company around the hearth.
scenes.adaptation: Local furniture and household craft remain dominant. A Wildhammer version has thick rafters, rough masonry and feather-colored cloth; other converts preserve their own family-house traditions.
scenes.purpose: Receiving kin and guests, discussing lineage, sharing mourning songs and negotiating family commitments.
scenes.lore: The native description treats ties among living relatives as equally important to ancestor ties. Wildhammer canonical mourning songs support a place for oral remembrance.
scenes.extrapolation: The dedicated family hearth, boards and furniture are a good-faith local venue extrapolation. Older RPG descriptions of communal lifecycle festivals are inspiration only; no fixed annual rite is prescribed.

10.label: Mashani
10.nativeMeaning: Mashani reveres the Earth Mother as earth and living nature, connecting shamanic and druidic practices with ancestors and the spirit world.
10.sourceDecision: A rites lodge and a modest life-and-remembrance preparation ground both have strong portable precedents in tauren spiritual practice.

scenes.label: The Earth Mother’s Rites Lodge
scenes.availability: the locality follows Mashani. A local community lodge, pavilion or covered teaching circle. Local Mashani faith. Scale to the settlement; an ordinary shelter suffices. No specific trial, vision potion or spirit manifestation is automatically active.
scenes.art: Build a broad teaching circle around painted posts or locally crafted supports carrying earth-root patterns and paired sun-and-moon emblems. Carved spirit representations, seed baskets, covered water jars and a partly finished devotional totem occupy the preparation side. Strong turquoise, red and ochre accents can distinguish a tauren-founded lodge, while converts express the same motifs through their own craft. Openings connect the lodge to nearby living plants and the actual regional ground. The roof shelters a teacher and a family group without cathedral scale. Give the circle, preparation shelf and smaller consultation corner separate useful positions under ordinary daylight and hearth light.
contexts: Root patterns rise beneath paired sun-and-moon emblems on the lodge’s supports. Seed baskets and water jars stand beside a partly finished spirit carving. The broad circle leaves room for teaching, receiving a family or discussing a proposed rite; a smaller shaded corner permits private counsel. Through the opening, the local earth and living plants remain visible. Paint, dry wood and fresh herbs scent the preparation shelf. The Earth Mother’s children and the community’s ancestors are honored within the same shelter, with the working objects close to the gathered company.
scenes.adaptation: The Earth Mother’s paired eyes and earth-life motifs survive in local craft. Tauren-founded versions favor painted poles and hide roofs; other cultures may use masonry, woven screens or a wooden pavilion without becoming a tauren village.
scenes.purpose: Teaching the rites, arranging a coming-of-age task, family consultation and discussing obligations to the land.
scenes.lore: GoA2 explicitly joins nature, spirit and ancestor reverence. The original WoW manual names painted totems and spirit lodges; the tauren rites provide teaching and vision-seeking precedent.
scenes.extrapolation: The exact lodge layout is authored. A partly finished totem and ordinary seed-and-water preparation objects represent ongoing community practice without automatic magical workings.

scenes.label: Pollen and Ash beside the Living Ground
scenes.availability: the locality follows Mashani. A tended sacred plot, family remembrance ground or sheltered garden court. Local Mashani faith. A small patch of local living vegetation is sufficient; identify ashes as ritual material without inventing a current death.
scenes.art: Compose a small tended patch of living earth beside painted spirit markers. On a sheltered low shelf, keep golden pollen in one covered vessel and gray remembrance ash in another, separated rather than mixed. Seed heads, a water jar, shallow planting bowls and a darkened ceremonial fire surface make life and death materially adjacent. A modest offering place and open standing ground permit family rites. Painted spirit markers face the small offering ground, where company can gather without crossing the roots. The plants rustle against their supports, and the old ceremonial fire surface remains beside the waiting vessels.

scenes.extrapolation: A combined small local preparation ground is authored. Adapting pollen supply to locally suitable plants is an explicit portable extrapolation, not an asserted canonical universal rite.

10.label: Candlism
10.nativeMeaning: Candlism treats the candle as wise and protective. Kobold origins make light, wax and a carefully defended margin against darkness the core religious motif. The native doctrine also permits human sacrifice.
10.sourceDecision: A candle-maintenance sanctuary is a distinctive mundane venue wherever followers live, including converted surface settlements; it does not require a literal Darkness monster.

scenes.label: The Candle That Must Be Kept
scenes.availability: the locality follows Candlism. A sheltered mine bay, cellar, cave or window-shuttered settlement room. Local Candlist faith. Choose a protected darkened venue where ordinary candles can safely burn. The sacrificial fittings follow the current effective human-sacrifice doctrine; omit that component if a reformed faith no longer permits it.
scenes.art: Give the sheltered room a communal candle larger than its surrounding personal lights, with sagging wax ridges, renewed wick bundles and painstaking little repairs. Smaller candle rests and wax offerings cluster around the base. Scrapers, spare wicks and covered wax pots sit on the maintenance apron, showing practical care as devotion. Warm gold flame meets the darkened doorway and high corners; the contrast should feel protective and a little obsessive. Kobold-founded examples use low shelves, sticky homemade fittings and scavenged supports. In other settlements, translate the fittings into local craft. Keep the flame ordinary and the darker recesses unoccupied. A separate stained sacrificial surface and dormant bindings occupy the darker devotional side, distinct from the wax work.
contexts: Wax has gathered in thick ridges around the communal candle. Smaller personal lights stand close to its base, with spare wicks and scraping tools laid on the maintenance apron. Dormant bindings and a stained sacrificial surface occupy the darker side. The room smells of warm wax and smoke. Beyond the flame’s reach, the doorway and upper corners remain dark. Visitors can bring wax, ask for a light or speak with the keeper while a fresh wick is fitted. The central candle is cared for as a protective presence; touching another person’s candle or taking a saved wax bundle is a conspicuous act here.
scenes.adaptation: Scale the candle to the community rather than copying Candle Rock’s unique giant. Kobold versions use lumpy improvised wax and low fittings; other cultures build their own holders and shelter while preserving the devotional importance of tending the flame.
scenes.purpose: Offering wax, requesting a flame, discussing supplies with a candle keeper and negotiating respectful access to prized candles.
scenes.lore: GoA2 makes candle wisdom and protection the faith’s central doctrine. Kobold game lore repeatedly ties personal candles to fear of darkness and records exceptionally large community candles. GoA2 additionally declares tenet_human_sacrifice, so the native faith has a darker ritual affordance than the candle description alone implies.
scenes.extrapolation: A portable communal maintenance sanctuary is extrapolated; its candle is locally made and not the unique Great Earwax Candle. No actual shadow monster or magical endless flame is introduced. The side surface and bindings are an extrapolated dormant preparation for the native sacrifice tenet, without adding a victim or a ceremony.

10.label: Fetishism
10.nativeMeaning: Fetishism is GoA2’s umbrella for poorly recorded local spirit faiths. Wards and rituals seek balance with nature, while the actual patrons and customs vary by people. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: A locally variable ward-and-offering recess is justified by the native description. It must preserve the particular local spirit rather than invent one standardized pantheon or universal liturgy. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: Bindings for the Local Spirit
scenes.availability: the locality follows Fetishism. A settlement threshold, sacred natural feature or sheltered devotional corner. Local Fetishist faith. Choose a meaningful local natural feature or boundary; patron identity follows actual local lore when known.
scenes.art: Create a compact spirit-facing recess around one locally meaningful feature: a living root, a wind-catching cleft, a spring’s edge or an ordinary stone treated with care. Knotted fibers, small carvings, painted ward marks and an offering bowl cluster at the boundary. Their material style comes from the local people; preserve deliberate handcraft and repeated maintenance rather than scattering anonymous occult props. A sheltered outer spot admits a visitor before they approach the bindings. Natural light and the surrounding biome remain dominant. Wards are visible devotional objects, with their actual patron and efficacy supplied by known local lore rather than invented glowing magic.
contexts: Bindings and small carved tokens mark the recess beside the respected natural feature. A shallow offering bowl rests beneath them, with fresh ties lying on a little repair shelf. The surrounding settlement remains audible beyond the devotional boundary. A keeper can explain the local patron’s place in daily life or receive an offering on the outer spot. Some objects are handled and renewed; others are left undisturbed. The arrangement gives the community’s relationship with nearby spirits a visible home. Fresh bindings wait in soft coils beside the weathered tokens.
scenes.adaptation: Use locally meaningful craft and material. Keep exact patron names and established symbols absent unless current locality evidence supplies them. A tree, wind cleft, water vessel or ordinary stone may anchor different local variants.
scenes.purpose: Receiving an offering, learning a local custom, asking permission before approaching a ward and discussing the community’s relationship with a local natural feature.
scenes.lore: The native description explicitly supports closely guarded local beliefs, rituals, wards and balance with the natural world. General Warcraft animist practices support treating places and natural features as spirit-bearing.
scenes.extrapolation: The venue is an adaptable fitting, not a named canonical faith institution. Specific patrons and rites remain local; the portable form does not claim that all Fetishists share its exact objects.

scenes.label: The Ritual Flesh Preparation Room
scenes.availability: the locality follows Fetishism. A screened local cult preparation room, covered feasting yard or inner devotional enclosure. Local faith belongs to one of the explicitly attached native cannibal-rite faiths and the current effective faith retains ritual cannibalism. The room can be dormant; an actual feast, victims and present contents of covered vessels require current scene facts.
scenes.art: Create a screened ritual preparation room with a heavy stained cutting surface, serving bowls, covered vessels and an ordinary washing jar. A low feast table stands deeper inside; the nearer receiving ground leaves room to speak with a keeper before entering preparation. The local culture supplies the construction and utensils. The selected faith’s own sacred motifs identify the rite: local-spirit wards, abstract cult marks, flesh-gift imagery, hidden deep symbols, seven-aspect patterns or blood-and-rot bindings. Preserve a grave bodily purpose rather than depicting an ordinary kitchen. The arrangement is dormant, with no person being harmed, compulsory meal, named corpse or magically compelled appetite.
contexts: A stained cutting surface stands behind the screen beside serving bowls and covered vessels. The washing jar occupies a separate shelf, and a low feast table waits farther inside. This preparation belongs to the faith’s ritual consumption of flesh, giving bodily offerings a distinct place apart from ordinary household food. A keeper can receive supplies or discuss a proposed observance from the nearer floor. Sacred marks frame the screen. Folded ritual cloth and washed implements lie beside the covered vessels, kept apart from household kitchenware.
scenes.adaptation: Use local architecture and the selected faith’s existing overlay: guarded wards for Fetishism, abstract forms for C’Thun and Twilight, flesh-gift symbols for Yogg, screens for N’Zoth, seven-aspect marks for Y’Shaarj or blood-and-rot fittings for G’huun. Respect current access and doctrine.
scenes.purpose: Receiving ritual supplies, negotiating an observance, discussing admission and conducting a conversation beside dormant ritual preparation.
scenes.lore: Each attached native faith explicitly declares tenet_ritual_cannibalism. G’huun’s blood-troll game precedents additionally document cult cannibalism; that racial practice is not used to infer every other faith’s rite.

10.label: Oachani
10.nativeMeaning: Oachani reveres its named pantheon and ancestors. Individual elders receive carved stone heads as bodies and homes, with ritual items and chanting guiding spirits to their rightful statues.
10.sourceDecision: Individualized stone elders are unusually strong portable religious architecture. A counsel shelter and a carving/preparation yard offer distinct uses without summoning a named ancestor by default.

scenes.label: The Stone Elder’s Counsel Shelter
scenes.availability: the locality follows Oachani. A settlement’s protected ancestor enclosure or communal devotional room. Local Oachani faith. Portray an installed stone elder without automatically producing audible speech, moving eyes or a spirit apparition.
scenes.art: Place an individually carved stone elder at the shelter’s inner end, with a specific expressive face rather than a generic threatening idol. A narrow ledge holds wrapped family tokens, ceremonial implements and a covered vessel. Warm lamps catch the tool marks and polished places left by care. The visitor side has mats or locally appropriate seating facing the ancestor’s body, with a small presentation surface outside the closer devotional ledge. A tuskarr example can use broad cheeks, worn tusks and bone rafters; converts give their own elder the appropriate features and building craft. Keep the statue materially still while making its personal ancestral status unmistakable.
contexts: The elder’s individually carved face fills the inner end of the shelter. Warm lamps show old tool marks and places polished by care. Wrapped family tokens and ceremonial implements occupy the ledge below it. The visitor floor faces this stone body, with a presentation surface before the closer approach. An inherited object can be unwrapped there, or a family’s concern brought to the keeper for ancestral counsel. The stone elder has its own identity and rightful place among the community’s dead; the shelter leaves room for the living to address it together.
scenes.adaptation: Founding tuskarr communities use walrus-faced heads, bone or timber roofs and warm woven furnishings. Converts carve their own actual elders with their own faces; the stone head as ancestral home remains the faith motif.
scenes.purpose: Ancestral consultation, receiving a family token, remembering an elder and presenting a concern to a keeper.
scenes.lore: Both GoA2 and the game quest Leading the Ancestors Home specify individual elder spirits, stone monuments and ritual objects used to guide them to the right statue.
scenes.extrapolation: The shelter and visitor arrangement are authored. Converting populations carving their own elders is a direct portability extrapolation; universal tuskarr faces would confuse religion with race.

scenes.label: A New Home for an Elder
scenes.availability: the locality follows Oachani. A local carving yard or covered memorial preparation workshop. Local Oachani faith in an inhabited settlement. Show an ordinary unfinished ancestral statue; a current death or completed spirit-guiding ceremony is not required.
scenes.art: Frame a partly carved stone head under a practical shelter. One cheek and brow are finished while the other side retains tool-cut planes, showing the labor of making a particular elder’s home. Chisels, stone dust, measuring cords and reference sketches occupy the work surface. A separate covered shelf protects the ritual implements and personal token used to identify the intended ancestor. Provide an outer position where relatives or visitors can examine the likeness with a craftsperson. Use local rock and architectural craft. The unfinished statue conveys reverence through individual workmanship rather than resembling an industrial stockpile of identical gods.
contexts: Stone dust lies beneath the partly finished face. One brow has its final shape; rough planes remain along the opposite cheek. Chisels and measuring cords stand beside reference pieces on the work surface. A covered shelf keeps the intended elder’s identifying token apart from the tools. Relatives can discuss whether the likeness is right, and visitors can speak with the carver from the outer work position. The future stone body is still being made, with ritual preparations protected until the community is ready to guide the ancestor into it.
scenes.adaptation: Local stone, tooling, body features and craftsmen’s furniture adapt naturally. Preserve a recognizable stone face and individual identification. Bone implements are a tuskarr precedent, not compulsory material for all converts.
scenes.purpose: Discussing a likeness, commissioning a memorial, negotiating craft labor and preparing a family’s ancestral ceremony.
scenes.lore: Native Oachani requires carved stone heads for specific ancestors and the ritual items to guide them into their rightful statues.
scenes.extrapolation: The carving workshop, pattern pieces and visitor position are ordinary spatial extrapolations from that documented practice. No particular ceremony or recently deceased person is forced.

10.label: Roanaki
10.nativeMeaning: Roanaki understands nature as a hard struggle. Its practitioners compel land and elements to yield, a forceful religious relationship distinct from reciprocal Mashani devotion.
10.sourceDecision: A command-totem ground represents that distinctive practice without assuming all adherents use Decay or automatically imprisoning a visible elemental.

scenes.label: The Elements Held to Terms
scenes.availability: the locality follows Roanaki. A local shamanic working yard, exposed sacred court or protected ritual shelter. Local Roanaki faith. Select ordinary dormant ritual apparatus; live bound elementals or active harvesting of their energy need current evidence.
scenes.art: Raise a strongly braced command totem over hard local ground. Tight ceremonial cords, heavy anchoring stones, a broad drum and lidded ritual vessels give the arrangement the sense of natural forces being held to terms. Deep outward-facing cuts and severe red-black bindings distinguish it from a gentle nature pavilion. A taunka-founded yard can use horn brackets and dark hide screens; other cultures translate the working apparatus into their own wood, stone and metal. The nearby biome supplies the actual environmental struggle. Ordinary fire warms the preparation side, while the totem remains dormant rather than displaying a chained spirit or corrupted elemental.
contexts: Tight bindings run from the command totem toward heavy anchors in the ground. The broad drum and lidded vessels occupy a protected preparation place beneath its outward-facing carvings. The local weather sounds beyond the screen. Here, a shaman can set terms for a working, explain a demand made upon the elements or receive a request from the settlement. The apparatus emphasizes control earned through struggle. An outer receiving position leaves visitors within sight of the totem while keeping the closer ritual ground clear for its keeper.
scenes.adaptation: Taunka-founded examples use heavy horn-braced wood, dark hides and red-black paint. Converts retain their own craft. Cold is a founding influence, not required weather; the same severe control motif can face drought, storms or dangerous local ground.
scenes.purpose: Discussing demands on local elements, preparing a working, receiving community requests and examining a shaman’s apparatus.
scenes.lore: GoA2 and taunka lore explicitly distinguish forcing the land and elements to yield. The Power of the Elements game quest supplies a Windsoul Totem that gathers slain elemental energy. Native Roanaki also approves elemental Decay magic; that permits current practitioners to use it but does not guarantee active corruption at every command ground.
scenes.extrapolation: The command-yard arrangement and visual bindings are authored representations. They are not asserted canonical physical shackles; Roanaki is not automatically equated with Decay-using dark shamanism.

10.label: Salamandrism
10.nativeMeaning: Salamandrism venerates immense fire-breathing reptiles as masters of the underground food chain, seeking strength and environmental mastery from their example.
10.sourceDecision: The native faith supports a salamander-effigy and offering ground even outside salamander habitat. Actual live-beast lairs remain conditional rather than following every conversion.

scenes.label: Claws of the Fire-Breathing Master
scenes.availability: the locality follows Salamandrism. A cave shrine, sheltered rock enclosure or settlement devotional recess. Local Salamandrist faith. The salamander is represented by carvings and votive objects; no living reptile or volcanic climate is required.
scenes.art: Make an immense salamander head and blunt predatory claws dominate a compact rock-sided shrine. Thick scale patterns, a heavy tail coil and painted fire marks give the reptile bodily power rather than turning it into a delicate serpentine god. Bowls of cold ash and blackened food-offering surfaces occupy the low devotional apron, with a small ordinary brazier nearby. Teeth and claws can be carved votives instead of actual rare beast remains. Use the local culture’s craft and a sheltered setting suited to the biome. Preserve the sense of an admired master of the food chain without adding a live salamander, lava cavern or compulsory sacrifice.
contexts: The carved salamander’s broad jaws overlook the blackened offering surface. Heavy claws and scale marks spread along the wall toward its coiled tail. Cold ash fills the bowls below them. A small brazier gives the nearer stone an amber edge, leaving the reptile’s upper form in shadow. Food and carved trophies can be presented here while worshippers speak of strength and mastery of harsh ground. The outer apron gives visitors a place to examine the workmanship or approach its keeper before entering the closer devotional space.
scenes.adaptation: Local culture can carve or paint the reptile rather than adopting trogg workmanship. Preserve thick limbs, broad predatory jaws and fire imagery. Trophies may be carved substitutes where actual salamander remains are not locally supported.
scenes.purpose: Presenting food or trophies, discussing strength and local survival, receiving a shaman and examining devotional carvings.
scenes.lore: GoA2 explicitly adopts salamander veneration as this faith. Warcraft III establishes giant fire-breathing salamanders; the trogg-worship and use-of-remains details derive from the older Warcraft RPG material.
scenes.extrapolation: The portable strength shrine and carved substitute trophies are authored. RPG-derived practice is accepted here because it is incorporated into the native GoA2 faith, not relabeled as current standalone WoW canon.

10.label: Naraxism
10.nativeMeaning: Naraxism venerates great battle-worms, especially Naraxas. Feeding worms eggs and sacrifices links devotion to the strength of dangerous creatures used in war.
10.sourceDecision: A local symbolic worm-offering shrine can spread with the faith. A second husbandry scene is useful only where actual living battle-worms are kept.

scenes.label: Offerings to the Mother of Worms
scenes.availability: the locality follows Naraxism. A settlement shrine or sheltered rock devotional apron. Local Naraxist faith. Symbolic image and ordinary offerings suffice; Naraxas herself and living battle-worms are not automatically present.
scenes.art: Build a compact devotional court around a carved worm maw with concentric teeth and a thick coiling body. Heavy bowls and feeding baskets sit below the mouth, accompanied by egg-shaped votive stones and ordinary meat or egg offerings appropriate to the settlement. Deep mineral colors and amber lamps can suit a rock enclosure; open-air versions retain local daylight and a protective roof. Preserve the formidable appetite and battle-strength imagery of Naraxism. The local craft and worshippers’ body scale govern the furnishings. This is an image of the Mother of Worms, not a transported Naraxas or an enormous inhabited pit produced by county conversion.
contexts: Concentric carved teeth frame the worm’s open mouth above heavy offering bowls. Egg-shaped stones lie beside the feeding baskets, and the body coils along the wall. The image joins appetite to strength: offerings are prepared with the great worms’ growth and power in mind. A keeper can receive a basket, discuss a promised offering or explain the carved maw to a visitor. The outer apron remains level and open, bringing company close to the heavy bowls. Lamplight catches the baskets’ thick weave beneath the toothed carving.
scenes.adaptation: Drogbar-founded versions use enormous rough stone bowls and deeply worked cave rock. Converts use local carving and baskets at their own scale. Avoid a colossal actual burrow unless geography and living worm husbandry support it.
scenes.purpose: Preparing offerings, receiving baskets, discussing devotional commitments and explaining battle-worm imagery.
scenes.lore: The native faith and official Legion dungeon preview document Naraxas worship; the Eagle Egg Recovery game quest documents feeding fledgling battle-worms eagle eggs.
scenes.extrapolation: The small local symbolic shrine and egg-shaped votives are portable extrapolations. A replica maw is devotional craft, not a second Naraxas or a claim that worms inhabit every locality.

scenes.label: The Battle-Worm Feeding Enclosure
scenes.availability: the locality follows Naraxism. A local battle-worm husbandry enclosure with suitable ground, food supply and handlers. Local Naraxist faith and actual current living battle-worm husbandry. Select only where local or imported worms are established; eggs may be locally sourced or supplied. Use normal current animals, not Naraxas.
scenes.art: Show an established enclosure for living battle-worms, with a stout feeding chute and a raised handler platform kept beyond the animals’ reachable mouths. Thick baskets contain the actual supplied eggs beside covered feed vessels. Worm-maw carvings and worn devotional marks merge animal husbandry with faith. Frame one currently kept worm only to the scale and condition supported by the locality; reserve Naraxas’s unique size and identity for her own site. 10.label: Twilight's Hammer Cult
10.nativeMeaning: Twilight’s Hammer proclaims the Hour of Twilight and seeks the world’s destruction in service to the Old Gods. Its cult combines apocalyptic preaching, ranked ritual life and elemental dealings. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: A local doomsday oratory is fully portable. A material elemental-ritual court is a useful secondary venue without copying Silithus’s functional wind stones or guaranteeing successful ascension. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: The Hour of Twilight Oratory
scenes.availability: the locality follows Twilight's Hammer Cult. A local cult hall, roofed camp assembly or occupied devotional room. Local Twilight’s Hammer faith. Display material cult iconography; actual Old God whispers, attacks and a world-ending event require current facts.
scenes.art: Make a hammer-marked banner and a jagged dark speaking platform dominate a local assembly space. Hooded ritual garments hang beside ranked medallion fittings, while apocalyptic tablets and copied texts crowd a preparation stand. Sharp black-purple painted edges and red-brown lamplight carry the cult’s severe identity without magical atmosphere washing out the local architecture. A broad facing floor admits instruction and proclamation; a narrower side recess allows a visitor or petitioner to be received before joining the gathering. scenes.label: The Four Elements before Twilight
scenes.availability: the locality follows Twilight's Hammer Cult. A local cult ritual court or sheltered working chamber. Local Twilight’s Hammer faith. Baseline is ordinary ritual vessels and dormant cult apparatus. Functional wind stones, summoned elementals and actual ascendants require present evidence.
scenes.art: Arrange four modest material stations around a dormant central slab: an ordinary brazier, a water vessel, a rough standing stone and a wind-facing frame with hanging cords. Hammer marks and sharp black-purple paint bind them into one cult working. Medallion hooks and folded ritual cloth sit on a side preparation rack. The image should retain the Twilight cult’s dangerous aspiration to elemental power while displaying only ordinary objects. Use local masonry or timber rather than the Bastion’s monumental elementium. An outer receiving strip allows a keeper and visitors to examine vessels or discuss a proposed rite before anyone enters the central arrangement.
contexts: Flame, water, stone and hanging wind cords occupy separate stations around the central slab. Hammer marks repeat along their bases. Folded cloth and medallion fittings wait on the preparation rack, where a keeper can lay out the requirements of a proposed working. The central arrangement is dormant; ordinary fire and moving air give its material objects their present motion. Visitors can speak from the outer strip while keeping each station in view. The court expresses the cult’s reach toward elemental power through vessels that remain close enough to inspect.
scenes.adaptation: Adapt physical vessels to the local culture and available materials. The elemental scheme is portable; rare elementium architecture and the original Silithus wind stones are not.
scenes.purpose: Planning a rite, discussing rank or supplied materials, inspecting dormant working objects and receiving an admitted guest.
scenes.lore: Classic wind-stone rites connect ranked Twilight trappings to four kinds of elemental summons; Warcraft’s Twilight cult also practices elemental ascension.
scenes.extrapolation: The fourfold ordinary devotional apparatus is a portable extrapolation from those practices. It is not a universal functional wind stone or a guaranteed successful ascension mechanism.

10.label: C'Thunism
10.nativeMeaning: C’Thunism venerates an intensely malevolent god of madness and direct destructive chaos. Qiraji are his children, but followers need not themselves be qiraji. GoA2 gives the faith aniconism and ritual cannibalism, so its public devotional space uses abstract forms instead of a divine effigy. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: An aniconic devotional court can communicate C’Thun’s direct, overwhelming attention through a frontal axis and concentric forms, while a shared preparation venue accounts for native ritual cannibalism. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: The Rings of the Unblinking Witness
scenes.availability: the locality follows C'Thunism. A local cult shrine, enclosed hall or roofed altar court. Local C’Thunist faith with the native aniconic doctrine. Use abstract devotional forms rather than a divine statue; direct manifestations, Qiraji armies and mental collapse remain separate current facts.
scenes.art: Build an austere devotional court around a scarred offering slab facing a high bare wall marked by concentric abstract rings. Their alignment and hard frontal axis suggest relentless attention without depicting an anatomical eye or divine body. Pointed uprights, black-and-ochre surfaces and narrow ordinary firelight give the approach a brutally direct silhouette. Local artisans provide the construction; Qiraji-founded examples may use chitin-like geometry while converts retain their own craft. A smaller receiving side and covered ritual serving vessels provide mortal use. Keep the faith’s native aniconism legible through the empty center and abstract marks rather than a figural C’Thun idol.
contexts: Concentric rings mark the high wall beyond the scarred slab. Pointed uprights draw the devotional floor into one hard frontal axis, ending at the bare center. Ordinary firelight catches the edges without filling that emptiness. C’Thun is honored here through an overwhelming arrangement of attention and approach. A keeper receives visitors at the narrower side, where covered ritual vessels stand beside the preparation surface. Offerings can be presented at the slab, or an admitted visitor can remain at the side to discuss commitments before crossing the central devotional ground.
scenes.adaptation: Local artisans reproduce the abstract rings in stone, painted wood, clay or cloth. Qiraji-founded examples may use heavy insectoid geometry; converted communities retain their own craft. Do not replace native aniconism with a literal eye statue.
scenes.purpose: Receiving an admitted visitor, presenting an offering and discussing cult commitments beside an aniconic devotional arrangement.
scenes.lore: The native description establishes C’Thun’s direct destructive nature and Qiraji connection, while the actual GoA2 tenets declare aniconism and ritual cannibalism. C’Thun’s game appearance supplies thematic attention, not permission to install a figural divine image against the native tenet.
scenes.extrapolation: The concentric-ring marks, bare center and forceful court geometry are authored aniconic spatial design. They are abstract symbols rather than a literal eye, an established canonical C’Thunist rite or a copied unique temple.

10.label: Yogg-Saronism
10.nativeMeaning: Yogg-Saronism reveres death and fate and treats the Curse of Flesh as a sacred gift of transformation, rather than merely venerating a generic shadow power. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: A local flesh-gift devotional chamber can express the native theology through crafted images; real saronite, invasive whispers and transformation remain exceptional states. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: The Gift of Flesh Chamber
scenes.availability: the locality follows Yogg-Saronism. A local cult chamber or enclosed devotional recess. Local Yogg-Saronist faith. Depict crafted flesh symbolism and ordinary materials; actual saronite, living growth, visions or body transformation need current evidence.
scenes.art: Make one wall carry a deliberately unsettling crafted relief: rigid angular bodies give way to softened limbs and folds painted in flesh colors. Above it, a many-mouthed Old God image gathers thick teeth and knotted forms without becoming living tissue. Black-green cloth, pale carved stone and pink-brown wax contrast under low ordinary lamps. A covered offering stand and a smaller consultation alcove provide usable religious space. The local culture supplies the architecture and depicted bodies. Avoid making saronite a universal imported building material. The chamber celebrates flesh as the cult’s gift while remaining an ordinary built place, with no automatic psychic voice or mutation.
contexts: The wall relief passes from hard angular bodies into rounded limbs and painted folds of flesh. A many-mouthed image rises above the transition, its teeth picked out by low lamps. Covered offerings rest at the foot of the carving. The cult names this change a gift, giving a keeper a place to explain transformation, death or fate to an admitted visitor. The smaller alcove sits outside the central offering axis. Cloth, wax and cut stone remain visible in the figures; lamplight warms the wax folds and sharpens the stone teeth above them.
scenes.adaptation: Translate the relief into local craft and depict the population’s relevant forms without claiming all inhabitants are titan-forged. Colored wax, carved stone and paint provide bodily symbolism where rare saronite is absent.
scenes.purpose: Discussing flesh as sacred transformation, receiving an offering and consulting a cult keeper about death or fate.
scenes.lore: Native faith explicitly venerates the Curse of Flesh as a sacred gift. Yogg-Saron’s in-game body supplies many-mouthed imagery; saronite is his blood and therefore cannot be assumed harmless common decor everywhere.
scenes.extrapolation: The transformation relief, wax palette and local devotional chamber are authored extrapolations. They depict cult theology, not a current bodily change or canonical universal ritual.
