10.label: N'Zothism
10.nativeMeaning: N’Zothism venerates the hidden god of the deep, whose influence favors manipulation, deception and change. Concealed attention distinguishes it from C’Thun’s direct brutality. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: An inland-capable veiled whisper chapel can express hidden influence through physical iconography and intimate devotional access without requiring an ocean prison or actual telepathic whispers. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: The Eye behind the Veil
scenes.availability: the locality follows N'Zothism. A screened local chapel, cellar devotional room or enclosed cult court. Local N’Zothist faith. Physical screens and quiet conversation are sufficient; audible divine whispers, an acquired third eye, Ny’alotha or physical corruption require current facts.
scenes.art: Place a crafted eye behind overlapping dark screens so that different parts of its relief appear from different positions. Coiling tentacle motifs and a deep-colored ordinary water bowl connect the image to the god of the deep. Narrow consultation niches and a central offering space make quiet, partly screened exchanges possible. Low blue-green cloth and amber lamp reflections suggest hidden attention without luminous void fissures. Local craft governs the walls and furniture, including inland stone or timber chapels. Let the screen create the unsettling ambiguity: the eye is an image, the bowl is ordinary water, and the whispering voices can simply be people speaking softly.
contexts: Layers of dark screening partly conceal the carved eye. Its lid comes into view from the offering floor, while the pupil is clearer from one of the side niches. A deep-colored water bowl catches the small lamps beneath curling sea motifs. Quiet voices carry between the screens without exposing every speaker. An admitted visitor can present an offering in the middle or speak closer with a keeper at the side. The god of the deep is addressed through hidden attention and changing sightlines, with the doorway still visible beyond the outer screen.
scenes.adaptation: Use local construction and locally crafted sea imagery even inland. An ordinary contained bowl evokes depth without creating a flooded building or magically importing ocean water. Conversion does not turn the surrounding settlement into Ny’alotha.
scenes.purpose: Screened consultation, receiving offerings, discussing a claim or secret with a keeper and controlled admission to inner devotional space.
scenes.lore: GoA2 establishes deep-god imagery, whispers, deception and change. Canonical N’Zoth cults and the Shrine of Shadows provide precedents for concealed devotional worship.
scenes.extrapolation: The screened inland chapel, ordinary water bowl and changing sightlines are explicit spatial extrapolations. Human murmurs do not certify divine whispers or turn the local cult into a particular later-era faction.

10.label: Y'Shaarjism
10.nativeMeaning: Y’Shaarjism venerates the Beast of Seven Heads and the seven emotional aspects represented by those heads. His Sha are enduring echoes of his destructive essence. Its native doctrine includes ritual cannibalism, represented by the separately attached shared preparation room.
10.sourceDecision: Seven-head imagery and inscribed prayer have a direct game-artifact basis. A portable local prayer court can express that devotion without importing his heart, a Sha infestation or the Klaxxi institution. The shared ritual-flesh preparation template is also explicitly attached through its local_faith_ids.

scenes.label: The Seven-Headed One’s Prayer Court
scenes.availability: the locality follows Y'Shaarjism. A local cult devotional court or enclosed prayer hall. Local Y’Shaarjist faith. The seven heads are devotional sculpture. Sha manifestations, actual preserved Old God remains and mandated emotional states require current facts.
scenes.art: Arrange seven stylized snarling heads around a shared central devotional form, with prayer bands cut or painted beneath them. Distinct angular markings identify Anger, Hatred, Violence, Fear, Doubt, Despair and Pride without legible fixed scripture. The artwork is a cult representation of the Seven-Headed One, not a claim to show his complete canonical anatomy. Amber-colored resin and dark lacquer can evoke mantid examples; other local cultures reproduce the heads in clay, wood or stone. A low offering place and open prayer floor permit assembly and individual approach. Keep dark pigment, smoke and sculpted mouths physical rather than spreading living Sha across the scene.
contexts: Seven carved heads surround the central image. Prayer bands run beneath them, with separate marks for Anger, Hatred, Violence, Fear, Doubt, Despair and Pride. The low offering place leaves the prayer floor open. A keeper can explain a mark, receive an object or discuss the Seven-Headed One’s place in the faith. Smoke catches the mouths and recedes above them, while the carved bands remain close enough to examine. Devotion has given the seven aspects a material arrangement here. Thin smoke rises past the highest head, leaving the lower prayer bands clear.
scenes.adaptation: Local artisans choose sculptural media. Mantid-founded versions may use amber-colored resin and insectoid framing; converts keep their own architecture. Seven emotion emblems must remain those given by the native faith, without adding new aspects.
scenes.purpose: Studying a prayer or emblem, presenting an offering and speaking with a keeper about the seven aspects.
scenes.lore: GoA2 lists the seven heads and their aspects. The game archaeology artifact The Praying Mantid bears a prayer to the seven-headed one; the Shadow of the Empire quest confirms mantid worship of the seven heads.
scenes.extrapolation: The seven-head local court and aspect marks are authored devotional design. The game does not provide a fully shown seven-headed anatomy or mandate this exact rite. The original archaeology artifact and Y’Shaarj’s heart remain unique.

10.label: Azsharism
10.nativeMeaning: Azsharism venerates Azshara’s extraordinary beauty, magical power and sovereign magnificence. Her icon reflects the campaign’s actual history, including any transformation into the naga queen.
10.sourceDecision: Queen-images and local altars are directly attested throughout naga territory. A dry inland cult pavilion can reproduce the icon without replicating Nazjatar or assuming Azshara is personally present.

scenes.label: Before the Queen’s Image
scenes.availability: the locality follows Azsharism. A local devotional pavilion, court alcove, shore shrine or inland chapel. Local Azsharist faith. Choose Azshara’s represented form from current campaign history: an elven queen before her transformation, naga queen once that transformation is established. Faith alone does not flood the site or summon her.
scenes.art: Make the crowned queen-image the pavilion’s visual center, framed by graceful curving ornament and blue-green cloth edged in gold. Select her depicted elven or naga form according to established campaign history. A low altar receives gifts, with a ceremonial approach broad enough for worshippers and a smaller place where a keeper receives petitions or tribute. Naga-built versions can use seastone and overlapping scales; inland converts build in their own materials and retain a dry floor. Lavish polish and aristocratic symmetry communicate worship of magnificence. The image is locally crafted devotion, with no giant illusion of the living queen, famous palace or automatically functioning arcane projection.
contexts: The crowned queen-image rises behind the receiving altar. Curving ornament and gold-edged blue-green cloth frame its polished surface. Gifts can be presented along the ceremonial approach, while a keeper receives a visitor at the smaller side position. Here, Azshara’s sovereign beauty and power are given a local place of honor. Devotional petitions and tribute can be arranged before her image, with gift trays waiting beneath the polished carving. The host settlement’s craft remains visible in the supports and floor, surrounding the more lavish ornament reserved for the altar.
scenes.adaptation: Local culture supplies structure and ordinary furniture. Naga-founded shore shrines may use scale motifs and broad slithering floors; dry-land converts may use a carved crowned image in their own pavilion. Sea ornament is crafted, not evidence of underwater geography.
scenes.purpose: Presenting gifts, arranging devotional tribute, discussing a petition and being received by a local keeper.
scenes.lore: GoA2 establishes Azshara worship and her historical transformation. Warcraft III shows her altered devotional image; WoW’s naga settlements have carved likenesses and altars, including the Shrine of Scales.
scenes.extrapolation: Dry inland placement, receiving floor and local keeper are portable spatial extrapolations. The image’s historical form follows actual state rather than advancing the timeline; cultural converts need not become naga.

10.label: Xavism
10.nativeMeaning: Followers honor Xavius, the first satyr, whose pursuit of power moved from Highborne sorcery and Sargeras to the corruption of the Emerald Dream under N’Zoth. Their religious imagery can celebrate nature twisted into an instrument of domination.
10.sourceDecision: A locally made shrine to the First Satyr can spread with the faith; actual Nightmare infection and corrupted moonwells remain distinct physical states.

scenes.label: The First Satyr’s Thorn Shrine
scenes.availability: the locality follows Xavism. A settlement-edge shrine, secluded garden, grove margin or screened room within a Xavist locality. A small devotional venue is sufficient. Render nightmare forms as crafted religious ornament by default; an actually corrupted grove, well or dream incursion requires current campaign evidence.
scenes.art: Build a compact, maliciously sumptuous shrine to the First Satyr. A horned effigy crowns a low stone slab; black lacquer and crimson resin give carved roots a fleshy, thorned appearance. Cloth hangs in ragged curtains around the gathering space, and small lamps pick out sneering faces, hooked claws and sacred nature deliberately distorted. Covered offering vessels and a shallow stained channel sit on the slab. A side recess offers privacy from the main approach. The enclosure follows the locality’s construction, while the Xavist ornament supplies its profane identity. Keep the roots visibly worked material unless local Nightmare corruption is independently established.
contexts: A horned image of the First Satyr watches over the offering slab. Black-red carvings twist familiar leaves into barbs and clawed hands, turning the shrine’s natural motifs against themselves. Resin and lamp smoke thicken the air behind ragged curtains. Covered vessels stand beside a shallow stained channel in the stone. The central space makes an offering visible to the gathered faithful, while a recess behind the curtains allows a bargain to be discussed out of sight. Beyond the screen, ordinary local buildings remain close enough to hear.
scenes.adaptation: Use local wood, reeds, stone or metal for the enclosing architecture. In treeless lands, thorn-shaped carvings and dried branches carry the motif without planting a magically corrupted forest.
scenes.purpose: Offerings, recruitment, covert bargains and arguments over power, revenge or the profanation of nature; access is controlled by the local shrine’s attendants.
scenes.lore: GoA2 identifies Xavius with satyr origins and Nightmare corruption. Warcraft depicts the Nightmare through thorned black-red growths and Xavius through transformed, corrupt forms.
scenes.extrapolation: The local effigy, curtains and offering arrangement are an authored cult venue, not an assertion of a universal named Xavist ritual. Crafted ornament represents corruption without creating it.

10.label: Therazanism
10.nativeMeaning: Therazane is the Stonemother, a protective maternal ruler of earth elementals. GoA2’s description stresses preservation, stability and patience; its live tenets separately allow violent practices, so the venue’s protective stone imagery does not dictate peaceful behavior.
10.sourceDecision: Her recognizable stone-and-gem form supports a modest sanctuary to the Stonemother wherever the faith takes root.

scenes.label: The Stonemother’s Shelter
scenes.availability: the locality follows Therazanism. A local shrine court, sheltered rock niche, village sanctuary or temple side chamber. Local Therazanism and a habitable, accessible venue. Stones and ordinary crystals are votive materials; visiting elementals or bestowed magical stones require actual present context.
scenes.art: Center the shrine on a broad, seated Stonemother likeness assembled from brown local stone, its mass enclosing the space rather than reaching aggressively across it. Violet glass or modest amethyst pieces mark its jewelry and mineral folds. A low ring of fitted stones creates a sheltered devotional hollow with benches against the outer wall. Trays hold polished pebbles, clay tokens and mineral offerings. Local builders supply the roof, wall and weather protection, while the maternal effigy remains recognizable across cultures. Warm lamps catch crystal facets against rough stone. The scene is inhabited by ordinary worshippers and attendants rather than a procession of spontaneously manifested earth elementals.
contexts: The Stonemother’s broad stone likeness fills the sheltered hollow. Violet facets catch the lamps beneath her folded arms, and a low ring of fitted stones encloses the gathering ground. Trays of polished pebbles and clay tokens rest on the ledge before her. The thick walls quiet the street outside; mineral dust and warm lamp oil scent the air. Visitors have room to sit along the enclosure or approach the offerings with an attendant. Behind the effigy, the seams of the local stone remain plainly visible.
scenes.adaptation: A desert uses shaded earthen walls; a forest uses a stone plinth under timber cover; underground communities use a native rock alcove. Retain the enclosing, protective silhouette without importing Deepholm.
scenes.purpose: Petitions for endurance or protection, offerings, private counsel and communal deliberation within a physically sheltering sacred space.
scenes.lore: Therazane’s maternal identity, brown rock body and violet gems are documented. The source description supplies preservation and stability imagery; the active doctrine conflict is preserved in research notes.
scenes.extrapolation: A sheltered local shrine, votive pebbles and domestic-scale maternal effigy are reasonable spatial extrapolations, not documented standardized Therazanist liturgy.

10.label: Theradrasism
10.nativeMeaning: Theradras is the Kalimdor centaurs’ earth-elemental mother. GoA2 presents her grief and fury, her dark bargains and her corrupted lineage; ancestor worship, bloody feasts and strength are active tenets.
10.sourceDecision: A lineage altar and earth-mother effigy can be established locally without reproducing Maraudon, Zaetar’s grave or his imprisoned spirit.

scenes.label: The Wrathful Mother’s Lineage Altar
scenes.availability: the locality follows Theradrasism. A suitable camp court, settlement shrine, earth alcove or local temple dedicated to Theradras. County faith supplies the devotional identity. The altar can stand outside a cave. Any actual ancestral apparition, local blight or active sacrificial feast needs its own present context.
scenes.art: Use a blunt, massive likeness of the four-armed earth princess, cut from ocher stone with purple and orange mineral seams. Its hands surround a heavy offering slab, giving the sacred figure a possessive, consuming silhouette. Lineage marks cover stakes or upright slabs behind it; bones, horns and weathered ancestral tokens crowd the lower ledges. A shallow channel in the offering surface and a nearby feast hearth provide physical evidence of a harsh cult without staging a sacrifice. The local architecture can be a hide-screened camp court, timber hall or stone room. Keep Maraudon’s immense cavern geography and Zaetar’s unique grave out of this portable composition.
contexts: A rough, four-armed image of Theradras looms above the heavy offering stone. Purple and orange mineral seams cross its ocher body, and lineage marks crowd the stakes behind it. Horns, bones and worn ancestral tokens lie along the lower ledges. A stained channel cuts through the slab toward an earthen bowl. The feast hearth stands within sight of the altar, joining devotion to the place where offerings are divided. There is room to gather before the mother’s image or speak beside the lineage marks, away from the central stone.
scenes.adaptation: Retain Theradras and the named lineage in the sacred imagery even among converts of other cultures. Surrounding construction and visitors’ bodily scale adapt to local culture; a centaur camp is only one possible form.
scenes.purpose: Lineage claims, ancestral offerings, disputes over strength and status, and preparation for faith-specific communal feasts. The dormant venue does not select a victim or force any participant to feast.
scenes.lore: GoA2’s Theradras description and active bloody-feast, ancestor-worship and strength tenets support an earth-mother lineage cult. Maraudon supplies ancestral earth-temple reference material.
scenes.extrapolation: The portable altar, local lineage markers and arrangement of feast hearth are authored extrapolations; the native holy sanctuary is not duplicated.

10.label: Pantheonism
10.nativeMeaning: Pantheonists worship the Titans under Aman’Thul and regard themselves as guardians of Azeroth’s world-soul and custodians of the Makers’ works until their return. Their native tenets favor progress, astrology and pacifism.
10.sourceDecision: A devotional study precinct can carry Titan imagery and custodial purpose to new communities without granting them a Titan facility.

scenes.label: The Makers’ Votive Precinct
scenes.availability: the locality follows Pantheonism. A local temple room, open shrine court or modest custodians’ study attached to a suitable settlement. Local Pantheonism. Depictions, copied diagrams and ordinary craft instruments are sufficient. Genuine Titan relics or functioning ancient machinery remain tied to their actual locations and ownership.
scenes.art: Make the venue a lovingly constructed mortal-scale echo of Titanic order. Geometric bronze borders organize a panel of the Pantheon, with Aman’Thul in the leading position. A worked model of the nearby land occupies a low table beneath a star chart; measuring rods, copied diagrams and repair tools lie beside it. The enclosing building belongs to the current local culture, while ordered lines, sturdy joints and careful proportions carry the religious overlay. A modest altar stands within the study space rather than beyond an inaccessible machine vault. Ordinary lamps provide light. Treat every model and relief as an artifact of local devotion, not a miniature working Forge of Origination.
contexts: Precise bronze borders frame the Makers’ reliefs, with Aman’Thul set above the other figures. A small worked model of the surrounding land rests beneath a chart of the stars. Measuring rods, copied diagrams and repair tools cover the adjacent table; its edges bear the marks of repeated use. The altar shares the room with this patient work. A visitor can bring a damaged object for inspection, compare a local account with the copied records, or speak beneath the Pantheon’s images while the lamps shine across carefully fitted joints.
scenes.adaptation: Use local masonry, wood or metal for the room and fit the shrine to its community. Preserve precise geometry and the Pantheon figures; a small devotional model replaces colossal Titan architecture.
scenes.purpose: Custodial petitions, discussions of ancestry or the Makers’ purpose, astronomical consultation and community repair work. Any actual ancient-site assignment comes from the live location rather than this scene.
scenes.lore: Native faith gives the Pantheon, custodianship, astrology and progressive tenets. Warcraft’s Titans embody Order and are associated with shaping, forging, lore and early titan-forged works.
scenes.extrapolation: The small shrine, locally made land model and everyday custodial table are portable devotional extrapolations; they carry no ancient mechanism, prophetic certainty or Titan artifact.

10.label: Shenism
10.nativeMeaning: Shenists venerate Lei Shen’s conquest and stolen storm power as authority to continue the Makers’ work. GoA2 binds this legacy to merit through strength, pursuit of power and the conviction that its followers alone are fit to rule.
10.sourceDecision: A local shrine of imperial mandate and demonstrated merit can follow the faith; it need not bring Lei Shen, Mogu’shan or a functioning storm engine with it.

scenes.label: The Thunder Mandate Hall
scenes.availability: the locality follows Shenism. A local temple hall, shrine court or appropriately scaled public devotional room. Local Shenism. A Lei Shen image and ceremonial storm motifs suffice; all lightning discharge, soul engines, animate statues and named imperial officials need present campaign support.
scenes.art: Give the shrine a hard, commanding axis centered on a relief of Lei Shen wielding the storm. Angular lightning glyphs run through bronze bands, dark stone or painted local timber, with green mineral accents recalling mogu monumental art. Upright tablets record victories, offices and services to the Makers; their arrangement establishes rank without displaying a preselected living ruler. A raised lectern or low platform faces the assembly floor, and a substantial ceremonial bell stands to one side. The building’s shell follows local construction and scale. The thunder imagery is carved and hammered, with no permanent storm overhead, animate statue guards or imported Engine of Nalak’sha.
contexts: Lei Shen’s carved image raises the storm above the hall’s central platform. Lightning glyphs bind the surrounding tablets into severe, ordered ranks. Victories, offices and services to the Makers fill their inscribed faces, leaving fresh space for another name. A heavy bell hangs beside the petition floor, its bronze surface worn where hands have steadied it. The platform makes a claim audible to everyone assembled; the tablets offer a quieter place to compare achievements. Local workmanship remains visible beneath the Thunder King’s imposing sacred image.
scenes.adaptation: Translate the enclosure into the local culture’s ordinary construction. Preserve the Thunder King’s recognizable image and storm mandate; jade can become painted stone or green glass without exporting an entire mogu palace.
scenes.purpose: Claims of merit, contests over rightful authority, oaths to uphold the Makers’ work and public recognition of service. No automatic selection of the worthy or presence of Lei Shen.
scenes.lore: Native theology supplies stolen storm power, Titan succession, meritocratic supremacy and cult-of-strength tenets. Lei Shen’s canonical statues and imperial shrine architecture supply visual vocabulary.
scenes.extrapolation: A local mandate hall, merit tablets and ceremonial bell are extrapolations, not duplicated unique lore objects or a functioning Dark Bell.

Extrapolation: A local mandate hall, merit tablets and ceremonial bell are extrapolations, not duplicated unique lore objects or a functioning Dark Bell.

10.label: Suntouched
10.nativeMeaning: The Suntouched branch of Titan worship derives from the Amathet. Solar magic and preservation of the Makers’ works are joined to an exclusionary crusade against beings they regard as tainted by the Void.
10.sourceDecision: Amathet solar idols and obelisks are explicit worship and magic-channeling objects, making a small local solar shrine a strongly supported portable motif.

scenes.label: The Suntouched Solar Court
scenes.availability: the locality follows Suntouched. A suitable settlement shrine court, sun-facing temple room or exposed devotional terrace. Local Suntouched faith. Sunlight or ordinary lamp reflection illuminates the dormant idols. Active solar beams, purification weapons or genuine Titan controls require current magic/event context.
scenes.art: Arrange a small obelisk and solar idol around a bright radial disk, using gilded or copper-faced local materials. An aperture or open roof directs real daylight onto the devotional center; in a subterranean version, reflected lamp light supplies the same sharp gold emphasis. Stern geometric stelae and a visibly deliberate threshold organize the approach. Keep the worshippers’ assembly space outside the closest idol ring, with a side position where arrivals can address an attendant. The design should convey blazing certainty and selective admission. Adapt wall forms to local culture instead of copying Uldum wholesale, and leave the idols physically dormant until a separately grounded solar rite is active.
contexts: Light gathers on the radial disk behind the solar idol, catching its copper edges in a hard golden blaze. A small obelisk stands within the marked inner ring. 10.label: Odynism
10.nativeMeaning: Odynists exalt proven martial worth and the hope that a glorious death brings admission to the Valarjar in the Halls of Valor. The faith carries ordeal, commemoration and feast imagery without guaranteeing any mortal’s selection.
10.sourceDecision: Locally dedicated trial grounds and mortal memorial feasts reproduce devotional purposes, not the actual Halls of Valor or their spirit inhabitants.

scenes.label: Odyn’s Valor Ground
scenes.availability: the locality follows Odynism. A local shrine yard, training ground or open hall attached to an Odynist community. Local faith and enough usable ground for practice or assembly. A sparring trial occurs only if the current scene calls for one; Odyn and val’kyr are represented by carvings.
scenes.art: Set an image of one-eyed Odyn above a clearly marked practice floor. Winged val’kyr reliefs flank the shrine as depictions of the hoped-for soul-guides, while a rune-marked boundary separates the trial space from witnesses’ benches. Shields, practice weapons and a water barrel sit along the outer rail. Use the region’s construction and current inhabitants’ scale, with carved timber and massive lintels only where local culture supports them. Gold or yellow accents catch the lamps without making the room celestial. The architecture should invite a declaration of worth and the scrutiny of an audience. Leave the floor available for ordinary conversation until a trial is actually chosen.
contexts: The one-eyed image of Odyn looks down upon a rune-marked trial floor. Winged soul-guides are carved on either side, their raised hands pointing toward the patron. Shields and practice weapons hang beyond the boundary, beside a water barrel and the witnesses’ benches. Scuffs cross the floor where earlier contests ended. A challenger can stand before the shrine in view of the gathering, while companions remain along the rail. The worn equipment makes worth something to demonstrate here, even when the ground is quiet between trials.
scenes.adaptation: Vrykul communities can use carved timber and broad Nordic silhouettes. Converts retain their local hall forms and ordinary weapon styles; the one-eyed patron, winged soul-guides and trial boundary supply the faith identity.
scenes.purpose: Challenges, martial instruction, witnessing disputed boasts, preparation for battle and debate about what makes a death worthy.
scenes.lore: Native faith and Warcraft’s Odyn trials connect strength with worthiness. Val’kyr take selected worthy warriors to the Halls of Valor.
scenes.extrapolation: The mortal devotional practice yard, witnesses’ seating and local patron reliefs are extrapolated; its trials do not grant automatic afterlife admission.

scenes.label: The Hearth of Remembered Valor
scenes.availability: the locality follows Odynism. A local Odynist gathering hall, camp pavilion or shrine-side communal hearth. Local Odynism and a gathering venue. Use the everyday memorial hall by default; a current death can select a wake variant. Funeral ships require suitable shore and event context.
scenes.art: Build a robust communal hearth space dedicated to remembered courage. A relief of Odyn watches above a rail of inscribed memorial shields. Long or joined local tables hold ordinary feast vessels, and one small commemorative cup rests beside the memorial rail. A speaker’s standing place at the hearth allows deeds of the dead to be told within earshot of the entire gathering. Use warm firelight, worn table surfaces, cloak hooks and the region’s foods rather than a replica of the divine mead hall. The memorial furnishings remain even on an ordinary day. No dead warrior, celestial visitor, funeral ship or mandatory drunken brawl appears without present story context.
contexts: The hearth warms a rail of shields marked with remembered deeds. Odyn’s likeness presides above them, and a small commemorative cup stands beside the nearest name. Joined tables leave a clear place for a speaker to recount a life within earshot of the gathering. Cups, serving boards and cloak hooks give the room the familiar smells of food, smoke and lived-in company. Along the shield rail, a visitor can read an old boast or ask who earned it; the hearth holds space for another story.
scenes.adaptation: Local food, building materials and cups replace compulsory vrykul cuisine or giant furniture. The shared purpose remains remembrance through feast and spoken deeds; no coast or magical longship is required.
scenes.purpose: Memorial storytelling, wakes, meals among companions, disputes over reputations and connections between mortal deeds and the hoped-for Valarjar afterlife.
scenes.lore: A Jarl’s Feast explicitly shows mortal vrykul drinking, arguing and commemorating a leader’s anticipated service with Odyn; the Halls of Valor themselves contain celebrated feasting.
scenes.extrapolation: The enduring local memorial hall, shield rail and single commemorative cup are extrapolations. The source funeral event is inspiration, not a perpetually active wake or universal boat rite.

10.label: Holy Light
10.nativeMeaning: The Church traces its authority to Mereldar’s visions and teaches piety, kindness and justice through the Holy Light. GoA2 combines communion, holy struggle and monasticism, giving both communal worship and practical aid a place.
10.sourceDecision: Chapels and aid spaces are widespread documented Light institutions; small local versions are strongly portable.

scenes.label: The Chapel of the Holy Light
scenes.availability: the locality follows Holy Light. A local temple, settlement chapel, roadside sanctuary or modest room used for community worship. Local Holy Light faith and a suitable habitable venue. Use a modest chapel unless the location already supports a grander institution; named saints’ relics or miraculous manifestations require actual context.
scenes.art: Compose a welcoming local chapel around a radiant Light emblem and an elevated altar or lectern. A sacred book, pale cloth, ordinary candles and polished brass create luminous focus without requiring a visible miracle. Public seats face the center; a low side alcove offers a more private place for counsel. Leave a broad arrival space for muddy boots, armor, traveling bags and different bodily sizes. The enclosing walls and roof belong to the local culture, from a timber village room to a stone temple. A larger city may add colored glass and soaring height, while the smallest version keeps the same worship and consultation arrangement.
contexts: Candles gather around the radiant emblem above the chapel’s reading table. Pale cloth and polished metal catch their warmth, while the public seats face the open aisle. A devotional book lies ready for the next reading. Near the entrance, there is space for traveling bags and armored visitors to pause before approaching the sanctuary. The side alcove softens the sound of the larger room, offering somewhere to seek counsel without addressing the congregation. Wax, clean linen and faint incense mingle beneath the familiar workmanship of the local roof.
scenes.adaptation: A converted community can retain its building silhouette and materials. Local builders express radiance through gold, pale cloth or polished metal; Stormwind’s cathedral scale and human architecture are optional local variants.
scenes.purpose: Prayer, teachings, blessings, marriage or community observances, petitions for justice and private clerical counsel. Specific ceremonies follow current participants and events.
scenes.lore: Native Church theology and its monastic/communion tenets support communal devotional venues. Warcraft has chapels across human and other settled territories.
scenes.extrapolation: The portable chapel plan and adaptable furnishings are extrapolated from documented Church institutions; unique relics, named clergy and cathedral scale are omitted.

scenes.availability: the locality follows Holy Light. A local chapel-side aid porch, monastery guest room or community sanctuary with shelter. Local Holy Light faith and a plausible covered venue. Aid supplies and attendants are ordinary; serious wounds, disease, refugees or an active healing miracle require present story facts.
scenes.art: Create a practical aid space beneath a modest sign of the Holy Light. Basins, clean cloth, bandage chests and cups of water stand near a screened examination table. A food shelf and travelers’ bench occupy the public edge, keeping ordinary hospitality visible alongside care. The porch or guest room follows the local culture’s materials; cool shade, a warm hearth or protected ventilation suits the biome. contexts: A radiant panel hangs above the hospice’s clean worktable. Basins and folded bandages stand close to hand behind a cloth screen, while the public bench faces a shelf of cups and provisions. The covered space shelters travelers from the weather and leaves companions room to wait together. Footsteps and quiet conversation pass between the bench and the chapel-side doorway. A visitor can ask for water, bring someone for examination, or speak with an attendant at the table; the screen provides privacy when ordinary hospitality becomes a matter of care.
scenes.adaptation: Use shade and ventilation in hot lands, a hearth in cold regions, and local medicinal supplies. Preserve shelter, aid and privacy without automatically adding a cathedral or plague ward.
scenes.purpose: Seeking treatment, shelter or food; companions’ conversations while waiting; clerical aid and modest charity. Illness and miraculous recovery are story-dependent.
scenes.lore: Warcraft accounts explicitly describe the Church and Silver Hand healing the sick and sheltering war survivors, with continued aid in chapels during peacetime.
scenes.extrapolation: The particular porch and portable aid furniture are extrapolations of documented service; no guaranteed instant healing or epidemic is implied.

10.label: Scarletism
10.nativeMeaning: Scarletism interprets unholy creatures as punishment for humanity’s impiety and demands the fiery purging of them and other faiths. Its devotional institutions fuse monastic discipline, holy war and vigilance against heresy.
10.sourceDecision: Local militant chapels and examination thresholds follow an explicitly institutional, exclusionary faith; they can be severe without recreating the Scarlet Monastery.

scenes.label: The Crimson Chapel’s Examination Threshold
scenes.availability: the locality follows Scarletism. The public receiving edge of a local Scarlet chapel, shrine compound or adapted temple. Local Scarletism. Visitors can remain at the receiving threshold; deeper admission follows current local roleplay. An active interrogation, prisoner, execution or demon infiltrator requires actual present context.
scenes.art: Build a disciplined militant shrine with red-white cloth and a blazing flame emblem over its inner doorway. A roster desk and admission rail make the receiving space resemble a devotional checkpoint. Polished weapons and folded tabards occupy a side recess; a locked inner door and a bench facing the desk give the institution a severe practical hierarchy. An ordinary brazier casts sharp light across devotional inscriptions condemning impurity. Local walls, beams and paving provide the enclosure. The portable template ends at the chapel threshold, allowing guarded visitors to speak without placing them inside an invented interrogation chamber. Keep torture or purification implements for a separately grounded active institution variant.
contexts: Red-white cloth hangs above the chapel’s inner door, where a flame emblem catches the brazier light. An admission rail faces a desk of rosters and devotional texts. Polished weapons occupy the side recess; the waiting bench stands where an arrival remains plainly visible. Inscriptions call for the cleansing of impiety and the purging of the unholy. Prayers carry from beyond the door, while the receiving space turns an ordinary visit into a question of recognition, purpose and access. The desk is close enough for an attendant to hear a quiet answer.
scenes.adaptation: Use local religious construction and available materials rather than obligate human Gothic architecture. Preserve the faith’s cleansing flame, martial order and doctrinal scrutiny; racial admission policy follows the current local institution and population.

scenes.lore: Native faith explicitly prescribes militant purging. Scarlet chapels and monasteries are documented, and canonical inquisitorial institutions demonstrate severe scrutiny and worse practices.
scenes.extrapolation: The portable receiving checkpoint and roster arrangement are extrapolated. Their existence does not create prisoners, torture events, named leaders or secret demon control.

10.label: Argentism
10.nativeMeaning: Argentists reject heresy as a justification for suffering and defend life against evil. Their Light is personally interpreted, and their martial mission is inclusive rather than a demand that all visitors share one dogma.
10.sourceDecision: The documented diverse membership and chapel/pavilion arrangements support both inclusive devotional spaces and practical relief grounds.

scenes.label: The Open Light Pavilion
scenes.availability: the locality follows Argentism. A local Argent devotional hall, community shrine or covered pavilion. Local Argent faith. A simple local congregation suffices; do not infer a named Argent Dawn/Crusade chapter, tournament, military alliance or historical leader solely from faith presence.
scenes.art: Create an inclusive martial devotional space around a clear symbol of the Light. Pale and silver cloth, a shared reading surface and open seating give the shrine unity, while equipment racks and benches of differing proportions accommodate the actual inhabitants and visitors. A low partition creates room for personal counsel without sealing the congregation away. Armaments remain at the edge, and the center is kept open for prayer or address. Use the local culture’s pavilion, hall or shrine architecture instead of assuming a transplanted tournament pavilion. The atmosphere joins readiness with welcome, keeping prayer, personal interpretation and practical protection within one visibly usable institution.
contexts: Pale cloth frames the Light’s radiant symbol above the shared reading surface. Devotional passages carry personal reflections in different hands. Seats and equipment racks accommodate the company using the hall, with the central floor left clear for prayer or an address. A low partition shelters a quieter consultation space. The weapons remain along the edge, within reach without occupying the devotional center. Visitors can approach the common table with a request, join the open seating, or seek counsel apart from the gathering. The room’s arrangement brings protection and personal devotion together without assigning a single place to every kind of guest.
scenes.adaptation: Retain the local culture’s architecture and make furniture usable by the present community. Diversity can be shown through available sizes and varied gear without spawning every Azeroth race or overriding actual local demographics.

10.label: Khazism
10.nativeMeaning: Khazism is GoA2’s independent blending of the Holy Light with veneration of Khaz, Father of the dwarves. Its native underground-redoubt and Order-syncretic tenets support a strong, crafted sanctuary without making dwarven geography compulsory.
10.sourceDecision: A shrine joining Khaz’s ancestral/craft association to Light devotion carries the faith’s distinct syncretism into any converted community.

scenes.label: The Sanctuary of Khaz and the Light
scenes.availability: the locality follows Khazism. A local temple room, settlement shrine or sheltered sanctuary used by Khazists. Local Khazism. A durable devotional room is sufficient; underground placement is preferred where the locality supports it, but faith adoption does not create a mountain, dwarf colony or Titan artifact.
scenes.art: Combine a dignified relief of Father Khaz with the radiant symbol of the Holy Light above a broad devotional table. Hammer-shaped borders and deliberately fitted geometry join craft ancestry to spiritual instruction. Gold and blue accents, a sacred book, small worked votives and sturdy seats furnish the sanctuary. Where local geology permits, make the room sheltered and stone-built; elsewhere, a durable local hall can carry the same religious overlay. Avoid making the altar a functional forge merely because Khaz is honored. The composition should feel coherent and independent, with the Father’s relief and the Light given adjoining places rather than one erased by the other.
contexts: Father Khaz’s relief stands beside the Light’s radiant emblem, both framed by hammered borders and carefully fitted geometry. A devotional book rests on the broad table below. Small worked offerings show the hands that made them: a carved joint, a metal clasp, a piece shaped and polished with care. Gold and blue accents catch the lamps above the sturdy seats. The sanctuary gives worship, instruction and consultation adjoining places. A visitor can approach the Father’s image or speak by the reading table while the local building shelters both traditions beneath one roof.
scenes.adaptation: Use human, elven, orcish or other local building styles when appropriate. Khaz remains the represented sacred father; the converts do not need to become dwarves or enter an Ironforge copy.

10.label: Kirin Torism
10.nativeMeaning: Kirin Torism cultivates respect, wonder and deep study of magic. GoA2 includes worshippers of magic broadly and Lordaeronic adherents who retain Light devotion with arcane interpretation; esotericism, astrology and Order syncretism are native tenets.
10.sourceDecision: A local devotional teaching room with books and demonstration space reflects this faith’s core practice, while grand archives, official Kirin Tor posts and teleportation networks remain location-dependent.

scenes.label: The Spell-Teaching Sanctum
scenes.availability: the locality follows Kirin Torism. A local mage-oriented shrine, study hall or modest teaching room in a Kirin Torist locality. Local faith and a usable teaching venue. The shelf collection and instruments can be modest. Actual institutional membership, active wards, spell demonstrations and a functioning portal need current facts; Light devotional emphasis follows the community’s current interpretation.
scenes.art: Make a sacred place of learning rather than a palace of unlimited magic. Purple and gold cloth frame star diagrams and carefully copied spell formulae. A modest bookcase, lecture table and chalked practice circle organize instruction; measuring instruments and covered reagent boxes sit ready along the edge. Where the local congregation retains Light devotion, a small radiant panel shares the teaching wall with the arcane diagrams. The building and furnishings adapt to local culture, and lamps give the formulas readable warmth. Keep the circle inert and the books materially accessible, with the demonstration floor distinct from the visitors’ seats. No portal, Council of Six emblem or endless archive appears automatically.
contexts: Star diagrams and copied spell formulae cover the teaching wall beneath purple and gold cloth. A practice circle lies chalked before the lecture table, with seats kept outside its edge. Covered reagent boxes and measuring instruments stand beside a modest shelf of books. The room gives magical study the dignity of devotion: a lesson can be heard, a calculation disputed, or a visitor’s strange discovery examined in company. At the side table, smaller conversations can continue while the central circle waits for an instructor’s demonstration.
scenes.adaptation: Local walls and furniture retain the prevailing culture. The core overlay is reverent magical study and instruction; celestial diagrams fit the native astrology tenet. A small teaching shelf replaces an omniscient Dalaran archive.
scenes.purpose: Lessons, magical-theological debate, examination of unusual discoveries, scholarly petitions and counsel about arcane practice. Optional Light iconography is an asset variant, not forced universal doctrine.

10.label: Masonry
10.nativeMeaning: GoA2’s Masons arise from craft guilds, reject clerical and royal moral monopoly, and uphold freedom, equality and fraternity under a Supreme Being. Aniconism, communal possessions and anticlericalism favor a shared guild sanctuary rather than a conventional priestly temple.
10.sourceDecision: The mod explicitly supplies the guild-based religious philosophy, making a modest communal lodge a warranted extrapolation. Warcraft’s Stonemasons support craft-guild texture without establishing this faith’s rites.

scenes.label: The Lodge of Common Work
scenes.availability: the locality follows Masonry. A local communal guild room, craft sanctuary or suitable settlement meeting hall. Local Masonry faith. Modest shared tools and a meeting room suffice. Do not create a named Stonemasons Guild, Defias cell, secret degree system or mandatory conspiracy.
scenes.art: Give the lodge the beauty of well-made common property. A broad meeting table sits beneath an abstract geometric aperture or lamp lattice, with no personified divine image. Shared tool cupboards, sample joints, measuring instruments and posted agreements fill the walls. Seats of comparable dignity face each other rather than a priestly throne. Local craft materials give the room its distinctive finish: carved timber, dressed stone, metalwork or woven structural panels as appropriate. A side workbench connects discussion to making. The scene should invite collective deliberation and pride in skilled hands, with the Supreme Being approached through order and light instead of borrowed occult regalia.
contexts: The broad table stands beneath a geometric lattice of light. An inscription names freedom, equality and fraternity under the Supreme Being. Shared tools rest in marked cupboards, and sample joints show how the room was made. Posted agreements hang within easy reach of the seats, which face one another rather than a sacred throne. A side bench carries unfinished work and measuring instruments. Visitors can bring a dispute to the table, examine a proposed design, or ask to borrow from the common stores. Careful workmanship gives the lodge dignity, while its open arrangement makes being heard a shared concern.
scenes.adaptation: Use the local community’s actual crafts and construction. Abstract geometry carries contemplation under the Supreme Being; no personified god statue or imported real-world Masonic symbolism is required.
scenes.purpose: Craft disputes, shared-resource decisions, political or religious discussion, aid among members and debate over authority without scripted revolution.
scenes.lore: Native description and active aniconism, communal-possession and anticlerical tenets supply the religious basis. Warcraft documents elected craft guilds and collective grievances.
scenes.extrapolation: The lodge plan, light lattice, tool commons and agreements are transparent mod-theology extrapolations. They are not claimed established Warcraft liturgy or real-world Masonic rites.

10.sourceDecision: Documented Void instruction and study support a portable training sanctuary whose eerie tools and guarded practice differ from an Old God temple.

scenes.label: The Study of Disciplined Shadows
scenes.availability: the locality follows K'areshi. A secluded local study room, restrained meditation chamber or properly screened teaching alcove. Local K’areshi faith and a suitable contained venue. Inert diagrams, dark glass and ordinary practice equipment suffice. Actual whispers, rifts, void entities, transformations or successful magical containment require present context.
scenes.art: Create a quiet but uncanny school of restraint. Indigo-violet screens darken a local room around an inert dark-glass focus. Diagrams split into branching possible paths rather than converging on one prophesied answer. A narrow marked practice boundary leaves observers’ seats outside the working space; notebooks and personal grounding objects rest on a side table. Use crafted, angular shadow motifs and controlled ordinary light to suggest the Void’s danger without generating real corruption. The architecture remains local, from a stone chamber to a screened timber hall. This is a place to study and maintain control, so exclude enthroned Old God effigies, living tentacles and omnipresent audible whispers.
contexts: Indigo screens draw the room inward around a dark-glass focus. Branching diagrams spread across the study wall, each path dividing into further possibilities. A marked boundary separates the practice space from the observers’ seats. Notebooks and small personal keepsakes lie on the side table beside an ordinary lamp. The arrangement gives instruction and watchful company a place near the work, with room to step away from the focus and speak behind a screen. Even at rest, the dark surfaces and unresolved diagrams make mastery feel like a practice requiring attention.
scenes.adaptation: Local culture supplies the architecture and material craft. Dark glass can become polished stone or metal; a modest meditation alcove replaces Telogrus’s shattered world, ethereal machinery or an automatically open rift.
scenes.purpose: Instruction in restraint, discussion of competing possibilities, supervised study, reflection on disturbing experiences and bargaining over risky knowledge. No presumed Old God loyalty or automatic loss of sanity.

11.label: The Shield-Muster Yard
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement.
art: Frame an existing courtyard or village green from just inside its entrance. Put shield racks, worn practice posts, a broad equipment bench and tightly furled company banners around a cleared central strip. Iron-rimmed wooden shields and bright stitched surcoats carry recognizable human martial craft. Arathi fittings are plain and clan-marked; Stromic fittings favor red cloth and compact disciplined ranks; Stormwindian fittings add blue cloth, lion plaques and a polished veterans’ bench. Keep the surrounding local buildings intact. Morning light should pick out dents, replaced straps and dust underfoot. A muster roll and an open route board rest under the porch where a delegation can speak to the marshal without crossing a practice bout.
contexts: Shield rims knock together across the yard, followed by the solid thump of a practice blow. Spare straps and repaired armor cover the equipment bench beneath the company cloth. A marshal’s table faces the clear strip where recruits learn to keep their place beside another shield. Veterans gather near the porch, comparing scars in old gear and watching the newest attempts. Visitors bring a request to the roll table, arrange an escort or wait while an instructor finishes a correction. The yard makes military service a visible part of civic life, with reputation tested in work others can watch.
hybrid: Native IDs qualify. A hybrid with Arathi-family heritage or actual Arathi/Stromic/Stormwindian ancestry may retain this yard when it retains a shield-formation, chivalric or veteran-service practice. Existing Stand And Fight, Formation Fighting, chivalry or Reverence For Veterans can support that practice; unrelated bearers of those traditions do not inherit these signs automatically.
lore: The native Arathi and Stormwindian traditions include Stand And Fight; Stromic has chivalry and Highland Warriors; Stormwindian reveres veterans. Warcraft’s human kingdoms maintain martial civic institutions.
extrapolation: A modest courtyard that combines muster, visitor reception and publicly witnessed instruction is an authored portable institution.

11.label: The Grain-and-Hospitality Yard
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement.
art: Use the existing inn frontage, market shed or granary porch as the backdrop to a lived-in produce court. Group grain sacks, barrel-hoop repairs, two honest balance scales, cheese boards and broad baskets around a shared oak table. White linen brightens warm bread, apples and thick earthenware pitchers; blue or green household ribbons identify separate sellers. Wheels and harvesting tools lean within easy reach. A bell hangs from a small portable frame above a petition board. Keep the local landscape and roof silhouette rather than reproducing Southshore or a lost capital. Late afternoon light, flour on a sleeve and crumbs among the receipts should make the court feel like a place where commerce becomes conversation.
contexts: The smell of bread reaches the yard before the granary doors come into view. Sacks stand beside the balance, their folded mouths held shut with household cords. Sellers cut samples at the shared table while a clerk sorts deliveries against the day’s tally. A jug and clean bowls wait for travelers under the porch. Prices, labor, damaged wagons and the next harvest all find their way into conversation here. A visitor can buy provisions, seek lodging or bring a complaint to the bell table. Several families’ signs share the same shelter, making local standing visible in ordinary trade.

lore: Both native cultures carry Agrarian. Hillsbradian has charitable and communal features; Lordaeron contains farming settlements, and Hillsbrad Fields is a documented agricultural settlement.
extrapolation: The shared bell, hospitality table and portable family-market organization are local extrapolation from these agrarian cultures.

A broad-nosed rescue mastiff rests beside a shallow water dish, its leather harness holding a compact barrel. Red-brown wood, weathered iron and practical stitched hides make the equipment unmistakably used. Leave the surrounding settlement’s construction visible. 11.label: The Water-and-Caravan Court
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Stored or locally available usable water exists; stock scale follows current supply.
art: Set a Wastewander stopping court beneath tough striped awnings tied to an existing wall, roadside posts or a camp frame. Lidded water jars, leather waterskins and a guarded measuring ladle dominate the central platform. Pack saddles, repaired caravan wheels and dusty trade bundles ring a low bargaining carpet, while ropes divide waiting animals from the stock. Use sun-bleached reds, sandy cloth, brass buckles and sharply cast shade; in wet regions, move the stores under a roof and retain travel-worn portable furnishings. A marked slate records issued water and cargo claims. The water source can be an actual local well or imported storage; no oasis appears by magic. Make scarce supply the court’s visible leverage.

Whoever controls those lids has a practical reason to be heard.

11.label: The Ale-and-Reckoning Hall
11.cultures: Khaz Modanic, Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, Dark Iron, Frostborn
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Required current practice: Brewery.
art: Fit a recognizable dwarven ale hall inside an existing inn, guild room, tented compound or local longhouse. The portable identity is dense oak casks with iron hoops, squat stoneware or pewter tankards, heavy communal tables, a carved keg sign and a stout serving counter. Put a cooper’s repair stool, brewery tally slate and small warm sampling shelf beside it. Offer broad benches and adjustable stools rather than assuming every patron is dwarf-sized. Steam rises from substantial food, lamplight glows amber through beer and polished metal, and old spills darken the floor. Keep the original walls, roof and landscape visible. The social center is the common table, where workday deals, family stories and competing opinions about good ale are heard at full volume.
contexts: The tap thumps home, and amber ale foams against a row of iron-bound tankards. Casks crowd the serving wall beneath a carved keg sign; the cooper’s stool is littered with shavings from a repaired hoop. Substantial food steams along the common table, where a work crew can settle its account within earshot of three other crews. Visitors are offered a place near the counter before being drawn into a tasting, a story or a dispute about whose barrel deserves the higher price. The hall’s standing travels through its brew, its hospitality and the promises made across a well-used table.
hybrid: All native dwarven cultures qualify while current Brewery is retained. Hybrids with dwarven heritage OR actual dwarven culture ancestry and retained Brewery can keep this hall. Furnishings and drinks suit actual patrons, including undead or non-dwarven bodies.

11.label: The Assay-and-Craft Bench
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Current assay, mining or metalworking craft is retained locally.
art: Arrange a compact dwarven assay and craft receiving bench within an ordinary local smithy, storehouse or mining-camp shelter. A heavy stone tabletop carries ore samples, jeweler’s lenses, small scales, stamped metal bars and a neat row of calipers. Steel tools have chunky squared handles; carved knot-like geometric panels and bronze nameplates give the bench a dwarven finish. Beyond it, a working anvil and quenching tub are close enough to hear but leave clients a dry place to discuss an order. Warm orange forge light catches flecks in the mineral samples while the entrance supplies daylight. Preserve the local walls and terrain. The display should make material quality, precision and the maker’s long-earned reputation tangible.
contexts: Ore samples sparkle under the jeweler’s lens beside bars bearing the smith’s stamp. A craftsperson weighs a fragment, scratches a note into the order slate and lays it beside a finished fitting for comparison. The forge rings beyond the dry receiving bench, where clients can discuss a seam in a blade or a doubtful claim about a mine. Visitors bring samples, request repairs or ask what a piece of unfamiliar stone may be worth. Small, exact judgments carry considerable authority here: the weight, the join and the mark of a maker who expects their work to last.
hybrid: Native Khaz Modanic/Bronzebeard cultures qualify when mining/metal craft persists. Hybrids with their ancestry and current Ancient Miners, Metal Craftsmanship or an explicitly retained assay practice can retain the bench; the traditions alone do not assign dwarven style to unrelated cultures.
lore: Both native cultures have Ancient Miners and Metal Craftsmanship; Ironforge has documented mining and blacksmithing services. Dwarven visual craft is precise and material-focused.
extrapolation: The portable combined commissions/assay table is authored; archaeology may be discussed when known, without requiring a later Explorers’ League expedition.

11.label: The Gryphon Companions’ Yard
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Actual maintained gryphons and knowledgeable handlers are present. Safe landing/takeoff space exists.
art: Place a modest Wildhammer gryphon yard on an existing roof terrace, raised village platform or open stable court with clear takeoff space. Huge straw nests sit behind stout timber rails; saddle trees, feather brushes, feed buckets and thick leather flight harnesses cover the handling bench. Tawny feathers and muscular feline hindquarters make the resident gryphons instantly Warcraft-like. Blue-patterned cloth, carved wing plaques and practical hill-dwarf woodwork supply cultural identity. Keep surrounding local buildings and biome intact, even if they are human, desert or forest constructions. Daylight opens across the landing edge while warm shelter protects the nest side. Ground ramps and a visitor rail connect the whole yard, leaving wing room and a quieter table for entrusted-animal discussions.
contexts: Feathers drift across the handling bench as a gryphon shifts its weight in the straw. A keeper checks the flight harness against the shoulder before laying it beside the feed buckets. The visitor rail gives the animal space while a ground ramp leads to the quiet table near the nests. Riders discuss weather, trusted partners and the care owed to an entrusted mount. A guest can arrange passage, bring news from a distant perch or question why a companion has returned without its rider. The yard treats flight as skilled shared work, built around a bond that cannot be reduced to a hired saddle.
hybrid: Native Wildhammer culture qualifies where actual gryphon husbandry exists. Hybrids with Wildhammer ancestry and retained gryphon-partner husbandry may keep the yard regardless of their one live heritage. Actual gryphons, knowledgeable keepers and safe flight space are required; non-winged/non-dwarven converts use ground access.
lore: Wildhammers are documented gryphon riders whose close partnerships and husbandry give their settlements a distinctive practical feature. Their GoA traditions include hunters and family/clan enterprise, not a uniquely named gryphon tradition.
extrapolation: A small companions’ yard is an extrapolated portable form of documented Wildhammer husbandry; no Aerie Peak or ancestral sky shrine is spawned.

11.label: The Compact Production Forge
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Current metal craft and ordinary forge fuel exist.
art: Fit an existing local industrial shed or courtyard recess with a fiercely efficient Dark Iron forge. Blackened iron plating and thick red-bronze rivets armor a compact fuel furnace; a treadle bellows and ordinary driven hammer keep the production line working. Rows of cooling fittings, stout tongs, die stamps and a sharply ruled order board surround a dry commissioning counter. Glowing metal gives the scene its red-orange heart, with sparks rising into a practical flue and soot marking the working wall. Preserve the original building and visible local fuel supply. Distinguish the portable smithy from the unique Black Anvil: these are ordinary tools wielded with Dark Iron expertise, geared toward repeated strong components and the bargaining power of timely output.
contexts: The bellows breathes in short bursts, and the driven hammer answers with a hard, regular beat. Cooling fittings line the rack beside the die stamps; each batch is counted before it reaches the commissioning counter. Red furnace light catches soot on the riveted casing and bright edges on newly worked metal. Visitors can order a run of parts, negotiate a delivery or bring a broken fitting whose failure has become someone’s grievance. The order board leaves little room for ambiguity about quantities. Dark Iron craft announces itself through forceful workmanship and a shop that intends to keep producing.

11.label: The Working Prototype Shop
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Current practical tinkering skill and modest power/fuel are available.
art: Turn a modest local workshop into an unmistakably gnomish working tinker shop. Brass gears, copper coils, jewel-colored lamps and painted purple housings surround a rotating prototype platform. An absurdly elaborate articulated tea-pourer actually pours into a cup; a small self-propelled parts trolley rattles between labeled drawers. Multiple magnifiers, sliding rulers and a spidery adjustable tool arm crowd the central bench. Charred trial pieces hang beside revised diagrams, showing that cleverness includes failures worth studying. Keep the original local walls and roof, with a raised receiving counter and adjustable stools for different bodies. Bright task light and a little escaping steam make the mechanisms alive. The extravagance belongs to inventive problem-solving and ceaseless tinkering rather than sales slogans.
contexts: A brass arm pours tea with three more movements than seem necessary, then folds away as the parts trolley rattles past. Colored lamps blink above the turning prototype platform. The bench is crowded with lenses, revised diagrams and a charred component someone still considers useful. An inventor explains the next adjustment while a customer tries to describe the actual problem that needs solving. Visitors can commission a device, bring a breakdown or volunteer to witness a trial. The shop’s inventions work just well enough to invite another improvement, and every successful shortcut seems to open an even stranger possibility.
hybrid: Native Gnomereganian/Leper culture qualifies where ordinary tinker craft persists. Hybrids with gnomish heritage or ancestry and retained tinkering may keep the shop; a configured practical tinkering capability is valid because GoA2 has no unique native tinkering tradition. Physical body size and racial engineering abilities are not presumed.
lore: Blizzard’s manual describes gnomish radical engineering, and the Ironforge guide places working gnome engineers in Tinker Town. Native Gnomereganian culture values labor, merit and learning; Leper culture also keeps Hard Working.
extrapolation: The tea-pourer, trolley and small functional prototypes are authored examples of ordinary gnomish ingenuity. The Rationalism faith commons supplies devotional intellectual context separately.

art: Build a Mechagonian reclamation bay inside a local shed or open market workshop. Sorted salvage bins, bright enamel panels, exposed brass actuators and red-yellow-blue punch cards surround a service chair with adjustable supports. Small batteries and power cells sit in numbered trays; mechanical hands, hinges and tool fittings wait on cloths beside their repair notes. A compact walking mechanical pet passes beneath the bench while a rebuilt motor turns smoothly on its mount. Preserve the existing walls, ground and local light. Colored punch cards stand above the work bench, where a repaired actuator rests on a clean cloth next to its old broken casing. The adjustable service chair leaves room to test a tool fitting or maintain an existing mechanical limb. A small clockwork pet clicks under the counter. Visitors can bring useful scrap, negotiate an upgrade or ask why a perfectly serviceable part has been taken apart again. The bay turns discarded machinery into new capacity, with the craftsperson’s decisions visible in every exposed join.
hybrid: Native Mechagonian culture qualifies where reclamation/augmentation craft is maintained. Hybrids with Mechagonian ancestry and an adopted salvage-upgrade practice can retain the bay. Existing mechanical limbs require actual mechanical clients; the same chair may service tools and fittings for fully organic converts.

The bench can service a working machine, a tool assembly or an existing mechanical body. 11.label: The Measured Work Precinct
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Current stone/metal craft and precision maintenance capability exist.
art: Place a modest titanforged-style work precinct in an ordinary local quarry yard or workshop. An assembled stone grid, concentric measuring plate, squared basalt blocks and bronze-edged working slabs establish exact alignment. A survey arm traverses a small plate under steady blue task light; visible marked tolerances and matched fittings make the engineering intelligible. Use angular dark-gold trim, deep blue inset details and clean monumental proportions scaled to the actual users. Keep the existing walls and surrounding landscape. Visitors stand beside a dry sample table where a structural joint can be inspected. The scene carries technical order and durable workmanship through furniture and organization, without producing a titan installation, a world-changing engine or a sacred Makers’ precinct.

Squared stone samples and matched bronze fittings lie on the inspection table beside the work log. A craftsperson checks an alignment before the piece is moved into the yard. Visitors can commission a repair, question a measurement or ask whether an old structure can bear a new load. The precinct’s authority comes from durable work that can be examined. Even the route through its working slabs feels measured, with a clear receiving edge and each tool returned to its appointed place.

Hybrids with Titanforged ancestry and retained Metal Craftsmanship, artisans or a configured precision construction practice can retain this precinct. 11.label: The Chainwork and Great-Weight Court
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Current heavy-work/strength practice is maintained. Giant-scale primary imagery requires actual giant users or adequate lifting machinery; ordinary-body cultures use the scaled variant.
art: Use an open existing work court with heavy chain loops, paired lifting frames, stone loading blocks and a broad forge recess. Oversized tongs, hammer heads and ring fittings convey giant-scale work when actual giants are present; a raised consultation platform lets smaller visitors see a sample safely. Frost-giant fittings favor dark metal, pale stone, cold-blue carved bands and a practical communal order board. Storm-giant variants move emphasis toward challenging weights, a winner’s tally and rough trophy slabs. Retain local weather and geography: frost-origin craft can stand beneath warm-region awnings. Orange work light contrasts with daylight on immense scored surfaces. The spectacle lies in great loads handled as public work and proof of competence, rather than divine thunder or a summoned storm.
contexts: Heavy chain settles against the loading block with a sound felt through the court. A new ring fitting is laid beside its worn predecessor while the workers compare the match. Tools and unfinished pieces stand in ordered groups near the forge recess, leaving a clear space for the next lift. The consultation platform brings smaller visitors level with the inspection shelf. A guest can arrange heavy work, question a delayed repair or watch how a crew shares a difficult load. Strength is visible in the task itself, and public standing grows around those who can be relied on to carry their part.

Deep scores mark the lifting stones beside a tally cut into the court’s standing slab. A challenger takes position at the chain, with enough cleared ground for a failed attempt to end hard. The spectators judge the lift closely before a fresh mark is added. Heavy tools and claimed trophies lie beyond the receiving platform, showing what previous strength has accomplished. A visitor can negotiate difficult work, seek an audience or test a boast in front of witnesses. Here, impressive words meet an object that has to move; the resulting reputation can matter as much as the original bargain.

The hoist creaks as a crew raises the loading block, checking each chain before the weight is shifted. Marked stones and ring fittings lie beside the work tally, with smaller graded weights ready for individual trials. Visitors watch from the dry receiving shelf while a foreman compares a repaired part with the worn one it replaces. A guest can arrange difficult work, question a late delivery or see a boast put to a practical test. The court preserves a respect for strength through coordinated labor and publicly witnessed effort, even when that strength has to be shared across several ordinary bodies.
hybrid: Native Hodirson/Gymerir cultures qualify for current lifting/work practice. Hybrids with either ancestry and retained coordinated heavy-work or strength-demonstration practice can retain the court. The giant-size primary requires actual giant users or machinery handling equivalent loads; use the scaled variant for ordinary bodies.
lore: Frost giant smiths are documented. Hodirson GoA culture favors communal discipline, Loyal Soldiers and spartan; Gymerir favors Only The Strong, Talent Acquisition and Eye For An Eye. Warcraft storm giants are immensely physical beings.
extrapolation: The shared lifting court and strength-tally organization are inferred from native values; it is neither a divine memorial nor a duplicate of Fjorn’s unique anvil.

11.label: The Shorecatch and Salvage Court
availability: Available at working shore landing. Actual suitable shore and current fishing or shore salvage activity exists.
art: Arrange a skrog coastal work court beside an actual rocky or sandy landing. Massive net knots, heavy anchor fragments, rough fish-cutting slabs and salt-stained carrying baskets make its work physically emphatic. Large shells and coral-colored paint mark sorting spaces; an anchor-chain boundary leaves a dry barter ledge for visitors. Show seaweed, shiny scales and tide-washed stone, with local boats or packs in the background rather than transplanted Eye of Azshara ruins. Actual sea-giant residents justify enormous tool and catch scale; hybrid ordinary-bodied workers use smaller pieces or lifting frames. The daylight should be bright and wet, the sheltered store darker and crowded. Authority is conveyed through the size and ownership of the catch, not a compulsory sea deity.
contexts: A thick net is spread across the cutting slab, its knots still wet from the landing. Fish, shellfish and useful washed-up fittings occupy separate marked patches beside the carrying baskets. Damp nets and wet weed scent the air. The dry barter ledge puts visitors where the day’s catch can be inspected before anyone names a price or claim. A guest can exchange provisions, request help with a heavy load or contest who recovered a valuable anchor fragment. The court’s rough order follows visible possession and physical labor, with the shore’s wealth brought close enough for everyone to argue over it.

11.label: The Claimed Salvage Den
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement.
art: Use an existing cave mouth, abandoned cellar, quarry shelter or rough roofed recess as a trogg salvage den. Crudely secured tool bundles and mismatched metal scraps crowd low stone platforms; a dragged workbench, cracked crockery and someone else’s splintered door have acquired new practical uses. A heavy club rack and chalk/scratch ownership marks establish territorial control. A cleared central patch lets the den’s strongest representative receive an outsider before anyone approaches the stock. Keep the local architecture visible through the appropriated clutter. Low smoky light glints on a surprisingly useful intact tool amid broken things. The den should feel forceful, materially hungry and capable of rough work, rather than a generic harmless campsite or an automatic berserk attack.
contexts: A useful iron tool lies among cracked pots and bent fittings, tied to a bundle whose ownership mark has been cut into the floor. Scraps of several makers’ work have become shelves, braces and doors. The central patch is kept clear beside the heavy club rack, leaving an outsider somewhere to stand while a claim is heard. Visitors can bargain for a taken object, offer useful supplies or ask who has the authority to release a disputed piece. Value here is immediate and tangible: something that cuts, binds, shelters or proves difficult for another claimant to take away.
hybrid: Native Trogg culture qualifies where rough salvage/claim organization remains. Hybrids with Trogg ancestry and retained rough salvage, Ancient Miners or Battlefield Looters practice can retain the den. Do not assign trogg bodies or intellectual limits to converts.

11.label: The Snail-Race Circle
availability: Available at an ordinary maintained settlement. Actual maintained racing snails, feed and a suitable moist/shaded surface exist.
art: Create a modest drogbar pastime circle on an existing market terrace, courtyard slab or cave floor. Three curved racing lanes run around a squat central stone; tiny colored markers, moist feed trays and keeper baskets occupy a low preparation bench. Show actual locally maintained racing snails with mineral-colored shells and narrow shining trails, leaving their scale believable. Heavy carved stools and a winner’s tally slab bring rough drogbar stonecraft into a playful public setting. Daylight or practical lamps make the trail texture visible. The host region remains intact, with the race surface shaded or sheltered as needed for the animals. A small clear receiving ledge allows spectators to argue about training, enter a racer or settle a wager without dominating the whole settlement.
contexts: A shining trail advances across the first lane while the spectators debate whether the leading shell has actually moved ahead. Keeper baskets line the bench beside fresh feed and little colored markers. The winner’s slab carries a surprisingly serious record for such a slow contest. Someone adjusts a starting marker and the argument begins again. Visitors can enter a trained snail, bargain for a promising animal or wait beside the circle while discussing a more substantial matter. The pastime brings patient attention and loud confidence into the same small space, with every tiny change in position giving the crowd something new to judge.
hybrid: Native Drogbar culture qualifies when racing-snail husbandry is locally maintained. Hybrids with Drogbar ancestry and retained/adopted snail-racing practice may retain the circle without keeping Drogbar heritage. This is an explicit configured pastime because no native unique tradition key encodes it.

extrapolation: A portable modest race circuit and tally is extrapolated. Named modern racers, Glimmerogg politics and later campaign events are not imported.
