art: Frame an ordinary local courtyard around a broad ring of packed earth. Keep the original town walls or countryside visible, adding rough timber posts, thick rawhide lashings, dark iron brackets and several fiercely shaped clan banners. Practice axes and battered shields occupy one rack; personal weapons hang separately beneath trophy teeth and weathered horn. Low witness benches surround a clear speaking edge, and a squat water barrel and linen bundles stand beyond the ring. Show warm firelight or strong daylight catching red cloth and old blade scars. Optional participants practice with purposeful weight, while witnesses have room to watch a claim or challenge being answered. The space should feel vigorous, practical and publicly accountable, with no famous champion or predetermined winner.
contexts: A broad ring of trampled earth lies between scarred training posts and a rack of repaired axes. Clan banners snap above the witness benches. The dull crack of practice weapons carries through the yard, broken by advice, laughter and the occasional argument over a clean hit. A person seeking recognition can stand at the speaking edge and state what they have done; those watching are close enough to challenge an inflated account. Water and bandages wait beside the resting bench. Ordinary training shares the ground with serious challenges, and an old grievance can become very public once both parties step inside.

11.label: The Blackrock Forge Yard
availability: Available at a local forge, courtyard smithy or repaired work shed. Required current practice: Metal Craftsmanship. Working forge uses actual local fuel and ordinary metal supplies. Advanced mechanized equipment requires present technology; cultural adoption alone does not supply it.
art: Show a working smithy fitted into the local settlement’s existing workyard. The Blackrock addition is concentrated at the hearth: deep dark iron, massive square anvils, thick leather bellows, rigid tool ranks and a stern clan banner on a riveted upright. Freshly forged axe heads and armor plates rest beside repaired agricultural tools, while mold boxes and quenching tubs occupy a deliberately ordered working lane. Strong orange furnace light cuts across coal-black timber and rough local stone. A broad inspection plank holds a tested blade, metal samples and chalk measurements. Make the craft muscular, disciplined and plainly productive. The modest charcoal furnace is the center of the scene; the distant environment stays local, without a legendary mountain, giant furnace creature or industrial war engine.
contexts: Hammers strike in measured succession above the furnace’s steady roar. Axe heads, hinges and repaired tools lie in separate rows on the inspection plank. The workmaster turns a finished blade toward the light, checks its edge and listens to the ring of the metal before accepting it. Visitors bring damaged gear, argue over the quality of ore or negotiate which commission deserves the next firing. Apprentices keep the bellows moving and sweep hot scale out of the lane. Blackrock pride is carried in the work’s weight and finish: a boast about skill can be answered here with something solid enough to test.

11.label: The Frostwolf Pack Yard
availability: Available at a settlement edge, sheltered courtyard or caravan resting ground. An actual resident or arriving managed wolf pack and handlers must be present; otherwise use the clan mess/proving ground rather than populate empty kennels.
art: Compose a Frostwolf pack yard at the edge of an existing settlement. Low timber-and-hide shelters face a broad open exercise lane, with thick fur bedding, water troughs, chew bones and sturdy food hooks. Leather riding harnesses and repaired travel packs hang from a sheltered rail beside combs and a small care table. A wolf-head clan emblem appears on cloth and carved fittings rather than turning every wall into a new fortress. Show a few actual wolf companions resting, moving or watching their handlers; their scale and coats belong to the animals present. Warm lamplight catches pale fur and hide against the local landscape. Keep a clear visitors’ edge where introductions can happen before anyone enters the pack’s space, conveying long familiarity instead of a generic cage kennel.
contexts: A handler’s whistle draws answering movement from the shelters. Wolves lie on thick bedding or pace the exercise lane, their attention following familiar voices more closely than passing strangers. Harnesses and travel packs hang beside the care table, where old bite marks and careful repairs show years of use. A visitor waits at the outer rail while someone makes an introduction. Feeding, grooming and preparing for a journey keep the yard busy, and stories about a companion’s courage are told as readily as stories about a warrior’s. An unfamiliar smell, an injured animal or a disagreement over handling can abruptly quiet the conversation.

art: Use an existing settlement green or wide courtyard as a Warsong gathering ground. Add enormous hide drums in rugged timber frames, iron-banded striking surfaces, red-black clan cloth and tall banner poles that lean like spears above the assembly. The trampled central lane joins an equipment rail and a few saddle racks to a speaking platform only one step high. No particular mount is necessary in the base image; an actual cavalry variant can place current local riding wolves or other trained mounts along the outer rail. Strong afternoon light or firelight brings out hide grain, worn wood and bright cloth. Show the visual suggestion of chanting rhythm and compact martial momentum, while preserving the town’s original surrounding buildings and a broad space for watching, negotiation and approach.
contexts: Deep drumbeats pass through the ground before the gathered voices answer. Banners move above a broad lane where companies practice entering together, halting together and making themselves heard. Off to one side, straps are tightened and travel gear checked between rounds. A new recruit can learn the rhythm before standing with the others; a messenger waits for a break in the chant to be noticed. The speaking platform makes a boast, accusation or announcement audible to the whole gathering. When the beat stops, the sudden quiet leaves every shouted promise hanging over the open ground.

11.label: The Burning Blade Sword Yard

Fine curved or straight two-handed blades rest on sturdy racks beneath individual back-banner frames; their silhouettes are elegant but brutally substantial. Grindstones, oil cloths, repair tools and a broad quench trough form a craft edge, with small tightly sealed blazegrease pots set away from the hearth. A brief orange-burning practice blade may be held over bare earth by an experienced present practitioner, casting vivid light across the banner cloth and nearby metal. Keep the surrounding walls local. The mood is intense concentration and exacting technique, not an automatic demonic ritual or an enormous elemental-powered foundry.

A short flare along an oiled edge draws attention back to the bare ground, where its wielder tests control as carefully as power. Visitors can commission a weapon, request instruction or ask someone to demonstrate a claimed technique. An insult to workmanship is easy to settle with a close inspection, and far harder to forget.

Thick carved wooden faces hang above a low workbench covered with red, turquoise and ochre pigment bowls, bone beads, twisted bright cords and curled shavings. One side holds polished stone ornaments, coin bracelets and feathered earrings; the other has rough blanks, awls and repair tools. Customers bring a broken clasp, a favorite pattern or a request to make their family’s colors unmistakable. Finished pieces are held up to the light and compared with the wearer, while the maker argues over materials and payment. The customer ledge gives visitors somewhere to wait, examine a gift or listen as neighbors dispute who has earned the right to display a particular mark.

availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement.
art: Build a compact troll hunting yard beside a local settlement, keeping the surrounding houses visibly native to the region. Painted forked posts hold bundles of throwing spears; stretched hides and split-log targets stand beyond a broad, unmistakable throwing line. A thatched or cloth-covered side bench carries snare cord, hooked knives, whetstones and half-repaired traps. Hang a few real local beast skulls and horns as records of successful hunts. Red-and-white paint and bone tassels give the portable equipment a forceful tribal silhouette. Leave clear spectator seats and a separate path into the village. Show use-worn weapons, disturbed earth and purposeful maintenance rather than a decorative military museum.
contexts: A spear strikes the hide target with a hollow thump. Beside the throwing lane, hunters mend snares and test new bindings while younger trainees retrieve spent shafts. Beast skulls hang above the bench, each ready to provoke another account of the hunt that brought it home. Visitors are noticed before crossing the painted line; a guide can be hired here, a disputed hunting boundary argued out, or a boast tested against an actual throw. The repair shelter provides quieter company, though the watchers on its benches miss little of what happens in the open yard.

Heavy spearheads hang over a bench scarred by skinning knives. Thick hide screens shelter the repair corner, and square carved posts bear the hunters’ clan colors. A trial throw cracks against the target while companions inspect a strap, a chipped point or a trophy’s worth. The equipment favors hard wear and close attention to what survives a difficult hunt. Visitors can bargain for an escort or bring news of dangerous game; anyone proposing a contest finds the measuring stakes already set. Quieter disputes are taken behind the screens, within earshot of the watchers.

Broad shade covers the spear rack and the bench where hunters retie worn leather straps. Stoppered water vessels stand close to hand, while the open throwing lane lies bright beyond the awning. Sun-bleached carved faces watch over targets patched again and again. Returning parties lay out their equipment before describing what they found, measuring an ambitious proposal against the supplies it would consume. A visitor can bargain for tracking skill, challenge a hunter’s claim or wait in the shade for the next party to return. The keeper’s bench is a useful place to learn which routes have become dangerous.

11.label: The Drum Common

availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement.
art: Arrange an inviting but forceful troll drum common inside an ordinary local courtyard. Several broad hide drums sit under a side canopy beside smaller hand drums and hollow wooden percussion blocks, all marked with vivid angular red, teal and violet patterns. A central floor of swept earth or worn paving is encircled by woven mats and simple benches. Curving painted posts carry bead strings and bright cloth that stir above cups and covered food platters. Keep the original walls visible beyond the portable fittings. Evening lamps produce warm pockets of light against the cool sky. The composition should invite music, dancing, conversation and a public challenge without resembling a shrine or prescribing who occupies the center.
contexts: The first deep drumbeat carries through the common, answered by a sharper rhythm from beneath the canopy. Neighbors gather with cups and food, leaving the center open for dancers, a storyteller or someone determined to settle a boast in front of witnesses. The rhythm can swell into a crowded celebration or fall quiet when a speaker needs to be heard. Visitors find a place on the outer benches before being drawn into the talk. A missed beat earns laughter; a shouted accusation earns attention. Behind the instruments, the serving tables offer a quieter corner for agreements that need fewer listeners.

Drumbeats tumble over one another as dancers circle the swept floor. Painted grins watch from the poles, bright cords swing above the benches, and someone at the food table tries to keep cups upright while clapping along. New arrivals can linger at the edge, trade news over a plate or step into the circle when the rhythm leaves an opening. A quick challenge may become a game, an old disagreement may gain an audience, and an embarrassing misstep can be remembered long after the music stops. The canopy keeps room for those who prefer to watch and talk.

Sacred drumming follows the actual faith scene rather than being inherent here.

extrapolation: Treating the instrument gathering as an available common in other troll settlements is a scaled cultural extrapolation; the particularly festive Shatterspear/Jellyneck branch is explicitly identified.

availability: Available at a settlement or route halt with usable water access. Required current practice: Seafaring. Actual navigable shore, river or lake access appropriate to the small local craft.
art: Compose a practical small boatyard on an existing local landing. Two modest hulls rest on timber cradles, their tall prow pieces carved into fierce faces and picked out in red, ochre and turquoise. Freshly bound joints, coils of thick rope, drying nets and woven cargo baskets occupy a low work platform. An awning shelters pitch pots, spare paddles, cutting tools and a scratched loading table. Preserve the region’s real beach, river stones or built quay beyond the colorful fittings. Light glances off water and wet wood; the shade holds deeper rust-red tones. Keep a clear route for visitors and a believable launch slope, with no immense warship or fixed capital harbor in the background.
contexts: Rope rasping against wood joins the slap of water along the landing. A boat rests on its cradle while a repairer tightens the bindings beneath its painted prow. Nets dry above cargo baskets, and a shaded table receives bundles waiting to be counted aboard. Crews argue over the next crossing, the price of passage and whose work will be needed before the next departure. Visitors can arrange transport or follow a damaged boat’s story back to the waters that struck it. The boat shed provides shelter for a meeting, though those working outside can hear raised voices readily.

Patched sails shade the salvage table, where mismatched buckles, cut rope and water-stained chests await their claimants. A painted prow leers over a hull being made seaworthy again. Crews crowd around a scratched chart while someone counts shares beside the locked chest. Ownership is argued loudly: one sailor remembers hauling the cargo aboard, another remembers taking the risk that made it possible. A visitor can buy passage, recover a disputed possession or offer news of a profitable crossing. The repairers keep working through the argument, knowing every quarrel becomes urgent when a departure is announced.

11.label: The Chartered Craft Exchange
availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement. Required current practice: Zandalari Cities.
art: Fill an ordinary local courtyard with a compact Zandalari craft exchange. Arrange stalls on heavy stepped display bases rather than enormous pyramids; broad carved panels use fierce faces, angular borders and saturated turquoise, vermilion and warm gold. Jewel samples, worked leather, folded textiles and ornamental metal fittings gleam beneath cloth shade. A raised but accessible counter holds weighing stones, tied records and the exchange’s painted authority mark. Original rooflines and wall materials remain plainly visible behind the additions. Show a clear central route, side seats for bargaining and enough work-worn detail to distinguish the place from royal treasure. Bright day light should make the exchange feel proud, sophisticated and insistently public.
contexts: Turquoise cloth shades the stalls, and gold-edged carving gives even a small display the weight of an official presentation. Makers set out leatherwork, ornaments and folded cloth while buyers compare finish and price. At the record counter, a clerk weighs a delivery and asks whose mark guarantees it. An artisan may defend the quality of a commission, a traveler may offer an unusual import, or a local official may hear a dispute before it blocks the trading lane. The exchange welcomes profit and spectacle, but a claim made here is likely to acquire witnesses.

Do not make every Zulian-heritage culture a Zandalari city. Retain Zandalari public presentation and organized craft trade alongside the other parent’s shops and materials. A retained Zandalari Cities tradition plus source ancestry can justify the feature; it does not rebuild the whole town as a pyramid city.

11.label: The Generous Kitchen

availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement.
art: Show a welcoming pandaren communal kitchen fitted into an existing local inn or courtyard. A broad preparation table carries freshly cut vegetables, spice bowls and several enormous serving dishes. A black iron wok flashes above a hot hearth beside a bubbling soup kettle, stacked bamboo or local-wood steamers and a brick oven. Warm lanterns hang from lacquer-red brackets attached to the original beams, with teal cloth and neat condiment jars adding color. Keep a generous observer ledge outside the hot working lane and benches where neighbors can eat. Steam rises through shafts of daylight, revealing the room’s competent organization and exuberant food craft. The surrounding building remains recognizably local.
contexts: The wok hisses as a cook tosses the next handful of vegetables into the heat. Steam escapes between stacked baskets, and the soup kettle scents the whole room. Neighbors work around the broad table, trading recipes, chopping ingredients and arguing over what the dish still needs. A visitor is offered a tasting bowl before the conversation has properly begun. The serving ledge makes room for news, a request for lodging or a disagreement softened by shared food. Beyond it, the working kitchen offers small lessons and practical favors, with enough witnesses to remember who helped when the meal needed another pair of hands.

Native culinary-art where present backs retention, but ancestry alone does not make every later descendant a chef.

availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement. Required current practice: Brewery.
art: Create a modest working pandaren brewery inside a local outbuilding. One rounded timber vat and a copper-rimmed kettle anchor the scene, accompanied by broad ceramic fermentation jars, grain baskets and orderly racks of squat casks. Use red-painted brackets and a few teal decorative bands on portable furnishings while preserving the building’s own roof and walls. Warm steam crosses cool light from a shutter; the kettle visibly simmers, and clean ladles rest near a tasting counter separated from the wet floor. Display handwritten batch markers and small cups, with wrapped travel kegs near the door. The room feels lavish in its care and aromas rather than implausibly immense, giving visitors a clear place to taste and talk.

Visitors compare its depth, heat and finish while wrapped travel kegs wait near the door. A disappointing delivery can become an argument over ingredients; a successful brew can turn into a gift, a contract or an excuse to stay longer. The counter holds conversation apart from the wet working floor, though the brewer’s attention moves between guests and the patient business of the next batch.

A visitor may request instruction, test a claim of skill or seek an escort among the regular trainees. Conversation resumes at the water bench between exercises, where rivalry and companionship have ample room to grow.

11.label: The Hozen Gathering Scaffold
11.cultures: Jungle Hozen, Forest Hozen, Mountain Hozen
availability: Available at an ordinary inhabited settlement.
art: Create a gloriously untidy hozen gathering scaffold beside a local courtyard, reusing existing trees, roof posts or a stone shelter rather than replacing the settlement. Lashed poles support uneven low platforms, rope swings and hanging food baskets; a wide stair and ground benches provide straightforward access. Nets, fishing poles, fruit peels, repair cord and prized colorful scraps crowd a side ledge. Carved grinning faces and bold painted hand marks turn practical wood into exuberant decoration. Warm light picks out dangling ropes and battered cups against the region’s natural background. Leave a broad ground floor for bargaining, games and shared food, with visible storage lids and strong bindings that make the chaotic structure believable.
contexts: The ropes creak above the gathering floor as someone claims a better perch and someone below loudly disputes the claim. Food baskets hang within sight of the benches, drawing more attention than the battered store chest. Hunters return with news, a fishing net needs mending, and a boast acquires several competing endings before it can be finished. Visitors find a ground bench and an audience quick to react to a gift, a joke or an insult. A useful offer can quiet the noise for a moment; a disagreement can bring it roaring back while the rest of the gathering watches eagerly.

Heavy lashings hold the platforms against the shelter wall, above baskets that are checked whenever another party returns. The gathering floor smells of hides and stored grain. Hunters argue over portions while a keeper counts what has arrived and what must last until the next successful outing. Visitors bringing supplies receive close attention; those asking for a favor soon hear what the community expects in return. A heated claim can draw listeners down from every perch. Beside the secured store, the quieter bench offers room to negotiate a delivery, an escort or an agreement about the neighboring hunting grounds.

art: Fit a severe mogu levy-and-commission yard into an existing local courtyard. A heavy but modest stepped platform stands beneath crimson banners and broad bronze fittings. Portable stone slabs carry deeply cut orders and stylized ranks; work tables hold unfinished relief panels, pigment pots and carefully sorted tools. A clear petition lane faces the raised official station while the production floor remains visibly separate. Massive-looking guardian faces and storm-scroll borders provide the imposing mogu silhouette at an achievable scale. Preserve ordinary local walls and rooflines around the additions. Hard slanting light and red banners emphasize authority, durable craft and controlled movement, with benches and tools sized for the actual mixed community.

11.label: The Living Planting Circle
availability: Available at a local garden, common green, sheltered grove margin or irrigated planting court. Plants suited to the actual local climate, with ordinary water and soil access; an arid location uses a modest irrigated garden rather than spontaneous wild forest.
art: Set a lush but locally plausible growing circle into an existing community green or garden court. Curved saplings and woven branch screens define broad paths between seed trays, young trees, edible leaves and medicinal planting beds. A worktable of polished local wood holds cuttings, seed pods, clay watering bowls and beautifully sorted baskets. Branch-shaped seats curve around a generous central patch of ground, leaving open approaches for people with varied bodies. Fern, flower and leaf silhouettes create a playful living ornament instead of a formal shrine. Preserve the regional plants and climate: hardy conifers and blue-green shoots in cold country, shade pots and irrigated beds in dry country. Scattered tools and half-filled baskets make the garden an active place of care and conversation rather than untouched wilderness.
contexts: Water darkens the soil around young roots, and the shared table is crowded with cuttings, seed pods and baskets of fresh leaves. Voices carry between the curved planting beds as neighbors trade advice, seedlings and news from the surrounding land. A visitor is offered a branch seat with room to watch the work or show a damaged plant. Small creatures move through the sheltered edges, drawing quick attention from the tenders. Arguments about a path, grazing animals or a woodcutting boundary can begin with the injured growth laid plainly between the parties. The circle’s lively greenery reaches into the ordinary settlement around it.

Pale branch fittings and blue-green cloth shelter a table crowded with hardy seedlings, clipped shoots and bowls of clear water. The tenders compare the condition of each plant before settling it into the beds. Visitors can rest along the wide edge, where small baskets of aromatic leaves pass between neighbors with the day’s news. Talk moves easily from a damaged branch to the animals or travelers seen beyond the settlement. A disputed patch of ground can be considered with its plants and water needs close at hand. The garden’s carefully tended life gives this small gathering place a bright, companionable center.

11.label: The Ancient’s Root Guest Circle

art: Compose a meeting place around an actual living Ancient rooted beside an ordinary settlement margin. Its immense gnarled bark face and branch crown dominate the upper image, expressive and unmistakably alive; folded root-limbs leave broad ground passages below. Portable carved benches, a low stone consultation slab, seed baskets and botanical records occupy the shaded foreground rather than a constructed throne palace. Scale a path and visitor seats to ordinary mortals while leaving the Ancient ample room to shift or uproot. Moss, hanging leaves and sunlight through the crown give the scene living depth. The surrounding architecture and flora remain regional. The Ancient itself supplies the extraordinary silhouette, while the added objects make its resting place usable by neighbors, envoys and craftspeople.
contexts: The Ancient’s roots frame a shaded circle of branch seats and a broad consultation stone. Bark creaks above the visitors as its living crown shifts in the air. Seed baskets and botanical records rest within reach of the smaller seats, with a clear strip of ground left between them and the great root-limbs. A caller can lay out a map, an injured cutting or a matter concerning the surrounding land. Those waiting have space to speak quietly beneath the branches before approaching the central stone. Even a brief exchange takes place under a presence large enough to make the settlement’s ordinary roofs seem small.

Long violet draperies, slim gilded or silver-filigree stands and sweeping curved chairs give the room a poised ceremonial rhythm. The central table displays jeweled craft, a bound score, fine calligraphy and small crystalline ornaments arranged as a learned conversation rather than a merchant heap. A discreet cleared dais supports a musician, poet or a small controlled arcane demonstration, with seating positioned to see and to be seen. Warm lamps and cool crystal light play against ivory fabric and richly colored cushions. The silhouette should feel cultivated, old and assured, with art and scholarship visibly entwined. Regional timber or stone remains beneath the portable refinement.

A score, a carefully bound text and several jeweled craft pieces occupy the central table. Hosts introduce a visitor by their work, patronage or connection before finding them a suitable seat. Conversation turns between poetry, skilled magic and the merits of a new commission; a subtle correction can draw as much notice as praise. The quieter outer chairs allow a private offer to begin under the cover of a performance. Lamplight travels along the fine metal fittings while the ordinary room holds this practiced display of refinement.

11.label: The Feather-and-Scroll Hall
availability: Available at a local covered room, shaded courtyard or broad platform with ordinary stairs or ramps. Required current practice: Storytellers.
art: Fit an Arakkoa scroll-and-story hall into an ordinary local room or covered platform. Feather-fringed screens and layered dark violet, ocher and blue cloth divide the reception side from tightly packed scroll tubes and hanging satchels. Hooked carved brackets and birdlike angles give the furniture a distinctive silhouette. A low reading table stands before a semicircle of broad benches, while short solid steps or ramps connect any raised working platform. Warm lamps illuminate red, blue and black ink on unrolled accounts; their feather and geometric decoration may remain secular. A deep shaded roof and bundled portable belongings convey a culture of guarded knowledge and carried memory. Keep the local walls visible and the entrance usable by wingless people. This hall does not require Skyreach, a solar weapon or a flight-only tower.
contexts: Scroll tubes and hanging satchels crowd the shelves behind feather-fringed screens. A keeper unrolls an account on the low table, weighing its edges before settling into the telling. Listeners take places on the broad benches, where questions may interrupt the story but a careless retelling draws a sharper response. Visitors can offer news, seek a remembered route or ask to compare a disputed account with the stored record. The lamps bring colored ink into view beneath the layered cloth roof. A scroll’s provenance, the right to hear its contents or the meaning of an old promise can hold the whole room’s attention.

Native traditions may substantiate the named practice, but a generic tradition in an unrelated culture is insufficient. Any environment, resident or capability requirements also apply. Feather screens, scroll cases and oral-history practice can be shared with non-avian locals. Solid platforms and stairs are default; optional upper perches require actual flight-capable residents and still leave a visitor route below.
lore: Official Arakkoa sources document both winged and wingless settlements and scrollkeepers. Native arakkoa has storytellers, Ruling Caste and a learning tradition/fallback, with corrupted-Arakkoa clothing GFX.
extrapolation: A portable public-story and scroll room is inferred from carried records and scholarly storytelling; its ground-access form is deliberate for the native outcast-compatible culture.

11.label: The Thorn-Revel Camp
availability: Available at a concealed local courtyard, ruined outbuilding, cellar or camp-sized woodland margin.
art: Dress a concealed local yard, ruined outbuilding or camp clearing with maliciously sumptuous satyr revel furniture. Black-red cloth twists around thorn-shaped frames; gold scraps, polished horns and dark cushions make a low central gathering mat feel inviting and sharp-edged at once. Small braziers light narrow cups, herbal bottles, hand drums and finely worked flutes or string instruments. The herbal preparation shelf should smell and look intense, with bundled leaves and sealed pigments reflecting native medicinal-plant craft, but no automatic supernatural poison effect. Keep gaps in the screen through which the local approach can be watched. Warm red light, languid seating and cruelly distorted leaf ornament carry temptation and menace through camp-sized portable objects. No Xavius altar, summoned demon or enormous corruption crater is needed.
contexts: Pungent herbs and warm brazier smoke hang over the low revel mat. Black-red screens curl around crowded cushions, leaving narrow views of the approach. A cup is offered with a flourish, and a musician lets a bright phrase trail into laughter as newcomers are measured by the company. Compliments can conceal a bargain; an amusing story may be pressed until someone’s discomfort becomes the evening’s entertainment. Goods and promises pass across the central mat in full view of those reclining nearby. Behind the inviting cloth, the thorn-shaped frames cast long hooked shadows, making the camp’s hospitality feel like an invitation with an edge.

11.label: The Draconic Guest-and-Trade Pavilion
11.cultures: Green Dragon, Black Dragon, Red Dragon, Blue Dragon, Bronze Dragon
availability: Available at a local courtyard, sheltered terrace or receiving pavilion with broad open approaches.
art: Arrange a draconic receiving pavilion within an existing local courtyard, retaining its ordinary regional architecture. Sweeping screens and wing-patterned cloth create a dignified open reception side around a polished presentation slab. Add comfortable guest chairs, low broad resting mats and generous paths, making the space usable by a mixed community. Flight colors provide the portable identity: emerald green, deep red, sapphire blue, bronze-gold or black and copper, with scale-patterned borders rather than mandatory aspect statues. Wrapped goods, tea vessels, maps and small worked stones occupy separate trays. Where actual large dragons visit, extend the same arrangement to a broad clear outer landing platform; otherwise keep the scale suited to present inhabitants. The atmosphere should feel old, measured and attentive to the weight of words while remaining a practical shared venue.
contexts: Wing-patterned screens frame the presentation slab, where wrapped goods and a map rest on separate trays. Guest seats face the open approach, with broader resting spaces set along the outer edge. The host gives an arriving party room to settle before goods or claims are laid out for examination. Tea and a carefully chosen object can begin an exchange more easily than a hurried demand. Flight-colored cloth marks the venue’s community, while the local courtyard remains plainly visible beyond it. A question of passage, stewardship, ownership or a proposed undertaking can be considered here with both visitors and their offerings given deliberate space.

11.label: The Draconic Public Learning Room
availability: Available at an existing local library room, learned hall or sheltered archive with public reading tables. Active magical experiments require actual qualified practitioners. Timeways access, genuine temporal predictions or alterations require separately tracked capabilities and are not supplied by this ordinary archive.
art: Turn an existing local room into a draconic public learning place with carefully arranged portable fittings. Tall bookcases and scroll boxes surround wide reading tables, a keeper’s catalog desk and a comfortable tea alcove facing the ordinary window or balcony. Blue styling uses sapphire cloth, silver book clasps and orderly arcane diagrams; bronze styling uses warm metal, dated record cases, clocks and paired chronology charts. Small steady lamps illuminate binding leather, polished wood and precise handwritten notes. Preserve the regional walls and structural beams beneath the elegant learned objects. The scene should feel welcoming to serious curiosity yet exacting about evidence and the handling of records. Keep any demonstration circle small and ordinary; no Aspect throne, time portal, predicted future or repository containing every secret of Azeroth appears.
contexts: Blue-clasped books and carefully rolled diagrams stand behind broad reading tables. A keeper checks the requested subject against the catalog before bringing a volume forward; visitors have room to compare notes with tea close at hand. A small demonstration table holds the components of a spell under examination, with its workings laid out beside the written account. Questions are answered through records, tests and the limits of what has been established. The familiar room’s light falls across patient scholarly work. A disputed discovery, a damaged book or an unusual magical report can bring several readers into the same careful conversation.

Warm bronze clasps mark the dated record cases around the reading tables. A clock ticks above paired accounts of the same event, while a keeper sets out a requested chronicle beside its sources. Visitors are asked when, where and from whom a claim was learned before the matter is compared with the archive. Tea waits in a quieter alcove for those staying through a difficult question. The room favors patient attention to sequence: a name omitted, a date altered or a promise remembered differently can change the meaning of an entire account. Outside the window, the ordinary day continues while the records are examined.

11.label: The Flight’s Living Collection Garden
availability: Available at a viable local garden, sheltered community planting court or modest cultivated terrace. Actual viable horticulture using local water, soil and climate; no spontaneous biome conversion, Dream gate or dragonfire fertility effect.
art: Create a modest cultivated garden within existing local walls, with the present region’s plants carefully arranged as a living collection. Broad benches, seed-and-cutting cabinets, illustrated botanical labels and wing-patterned shade cloth give the place a draconic identity. Red-flight styling emphasizes scarlet flowers, warm copper and an inviting propagation table; green-flight styling uses deep emerald foliage, curling branch trellises and a shaded observation bench beside locally appropriate wildlife-friendly growth. Ordinary watering channels and clay pots make the care practical. Preserve the surrounding climate and architecture instead of spawning an Emerald Dream pocket or a miniature Life Pool. The image should convey attentive stewardship and the delight of living variety through well-used tools, thriving modest beds and spaces where residents can examine a plant together.
contexts: Scarlet cloth shades the propagation table, where young plants stand beside seed packets and careful botanical notes. The tenders compare which cuttings have taken and what each will need before being moved into the beds. Visitors find broad seats within sight of the work, with fragrant leaves and flower color brightening the local court. A neighbor may arrive seeking a hardy plant, help with a failing crop or advice about sheltering a small creature. Conversation turns easily from growth to the way the surrounding land is used. The garden’s living collection makes care a practical public activity, visible in every watered pot and repaired support.

Emerald shade cloth shelters the observation bench beside a tangle of carefully supported living growth. Botanical notes lie open near the seed cabinets, with small traces of insects and birds left undisturbed among the beds. Tenders compare what flourishes together, what crowds its neighbors and where the soil has begun to fail. Visitors can bring a cutting, a troubling field report or a question about the use of nearby land. The conversation follows the visible connections between plants and creatures rather than a bare list of yields. From the broad bench, the garden’s patient work is easy to observe alongside the ordinary settlement beyond its leaves.

11.label: The Concession Yard
availability: Available at an ordinary extraction margin beside timber, a quarry, a local mine or another already plausible workable resource. Choose a real local resource form from terrain or known resource/building data; an underground mine-face variant requires an actual mine context. Cultural presence does not create ore deposits, kajamite, Azerite or a named cartel.
art: Keep the local woodline, quarry wall or mine entrance behind a compact goblin extraction yard. An old shed has gained riveted sheet-metal skirts, a raised foreman’s booth and an oversized grinning coin sign. Dented hauling gear and an overpowered cutting mechanism crowd one side; stacked resource loads and a chained payroll window occupy the other. Yellow hazard paint, red sales banners, oily brass and soot make a violently cheerful commercial palette. A comfortable padded chair sits above the cramped labor bench. Place ore or timber samples on a weighing table in the foreground, with claim stakes and enormous promotional graphics beyond. Machinery feels useful, improvised and hard-driven. Leave room for bargaining between the samples, workers’ waiting rail and access to the operation.
contexts: The foreman’s booth rises over the yard beneath a grinning bargain sign. Machinery clatters behind the sample scales, and the smell of hot grease reaches the payroll rail. Loads are marked, weighed and hurried onward while laborers wait below a chair much softer than their own benches. A clerk can quote output, labor and hauling costs before a visitor has finished looking at the workings. Claim stakes crowd the boundary; complaints about damage, wages or ownership meet the same polished counter as proposals for expansion. Everything here is arranged to turn the surrounding land into a saleable load, preferably before a rival gets to it.
hybrid: Default to current Kezanian culture or an applicable living goblin heritage with local extraction context. A hybrid with other heritage can keep this venue through goblin ancestry plus retained mining, forestry or concession-enterprise practice; a generic Ancient Miners tradition alone does not establish goblin styling.
lore: Venture Company operations demonstrate the traveling extraction enterprise; native Kezanian Ancient Miners and Hard Working support a local resource-work template. Goblin commercial excess is broader than the Fortunist faith.
extrapolation: The reusable foreman/payroll/sample layout, miniature local machinery and unequal furnishing are inferred practical scene organization. This is an independently branded local concern, not automatic Venture Company membership.

11.label: The Guaranteed-For-Now Repair Shop
availability: Available at an ordinary workshop, lean-to, storefront or market-side shed with access to common tools and supplies. Represent locally maintainable common engineering, not a unique world-scale engine. Do not automatically start an accident.
art: Fit an irrepressible goblin repair shop into a recognizable local room or shed. Reclaimed metal walls bristle with unequal pressure gauges, spring traps, sputtering burners and a functioning pump assembled from several incompatible machines. A broad scorched testing plate faces a showy customer chair; behind it, parts are sorted in crates bearing wildly confident product pictures. Red-and-yellow promotional panels, gold-painted trim and oily green glass compete with dark grease and burn marks. A sales horn hangs above the fee counter, while a stout rail separates observers from the test bench. Show useful work in progress rather than a staged catastrophic explosion. Make the shop dense, opportunistic, theatrical and visually different from a gnome’s lovingly optimized engineering laboratory.
contexts: A pump chatters behind a sales horn while burners hiss beneath a row of confidently labeled repairs. The best customer chair faces the testing plate, where scorch marks outnumber the reassuring notices. Every loose part has a price, every improved part a higher one, and the warranty board has enough small print to shelter a very small rat. Customers bring failed devices, impossible requests and complaints that can become new commissions. The proprietor’s assistants recover anything the previous job left usable. A working mechanism can be inspected at the rail while an argument about responsibility, urgency or the premium service package continues at the counter.

Tar and hot metal mingle beneath the workshop’s patched roof. A squat pump coughs water into a barrel beside winch fittings, harpoon parts and crates of suspiciously versatile spare valves. The customer rail offers a dry place to argue over a repair while the slip-side tackle creaks beyond it. Rates distinguish ordinary service, urgent service and service performed before anyone asks awkward questions about the vessel. Shipping hands bring damaged gear and news of approaching cargoes. A fitting can be tested here without surrendering the whole commission, although the counter has several profitable opinions about why that would be a mistake.
hybrid: Use current Kezanian/Blackwater culture or applicable goblin heritage. Goblin ancestry can carry the familiar repair-and-upsell custom into a hybrid without a new construction flag; explicit retained workshop practice is required when the hybrid has otherwise moved away from this custom. Live bodies need not be goblins. Blackwater’s complete maritime variant is selected only for Blackwater lineage with a shore or shipping context.
lore: Blizzard documents goblin explosive invention, alchemy, scrap recovery and commercial resourcefulness. Kezanian and Blackwater culture are separate live goblin-heritage identities; neither needs the wealth faith to possess a technical business.
extrapolation: The small service shop, warranty satire and test bench extrapolate ordinary public engineering work. The culture supplies the institutional tone; no individual character must be reckless, greedy or dishonest.

11.label: The Blackwater Cargo Yard
availability: Available at an ordinary quay, navigable-water landing or coastal warehouse forecourt. Actual coast or navigable shipping water is required. No particular ship, pirate captain, fleet, seized cargo or slavery institution is spawned.
art: Overlay the existing dock or warehouse frontage with a compact Blackwater cargo concern. Stacked branded crates surround freight scales, rope tackles and a tall dispatch booth painted in brash red, green and tarnished gold. A conspicuously luxurious private waiting seat faces a cramped hiring rail. Wax seals, chalk marks and locked strongboxes cluster at the brokerage desk; ship timber and a modest loading ramp remain recognizable beneath riveted additions. Add jaunty pennants with maritime commercial emblems, not a universal faction banner. The composition should show both the noisy public loading side and the curtained desk where awkward consignments can be discussed. Actual harbor water supplies cool reflected light against warm lanterns and oily metal fittings.
contexts: Crates rise around the freight scales beneath cheerful notices selling speed, security and considerably more privacy. Porters queue at the hiring rail while the brokerage desk sits behind a curtain just thick enough to suggest discretion. Tackle knocks against the loading frame, and pitch-scented air carries the sound of water beyond the warehouse. A cargo can acquire a passage, an escort or a less conspicuous description here. Visitors with inconvenient questions find the public counter; visitors with useful offers may be shown the better chair. Dispatch notes and docking priority give the yard’s overseers authority well beyond the piles of merchandise.
hybrid: Current Blackwater culture is the native default. A hybrid can inherit Blackwater cargo brokerage from ancestry plus an actively retained seafaring, maritime mercantile or pirate-port custom; a generic coastal location or unrelated Seafaring tradition is insufficient. Goblin heritage alone does not make every goblin culture a Blackwater pirate port.
lore: Native Blackwater has Practiced Pirates, Seafaring, Maritime Mercantilism and Battlefield Looters. Blizzard’s cartel profile independently establishes a Blackwater shipping identity, but its modern luxury-vacation business and current leadership are not imposed across all eras.
extrapolation: A modest cargo brokerage with public and discreet desks is a portable interpretation of the shipping/pirate-commercial identity. It is not automatic membership of the modern named cartel.

11.label: The Painted Story-Pole Circle
availability: Available at a village green, existing courtyard, camp common or broad settlement meeting ground.
art: Set a bright tauren civic gathering circle into an existing village green or courtyard. Several tall carved poles stack emphatic animal faces and geometric bands in turquoise, red ochre, cream and dark wood. Their bases share the space with broad low benches, hide awnings and a partially carved history post secured beside woodworking tools. A large drum and beaded hangings enrich the perimeter while leaving a generous open center. Preserve the surrounding local houses rather than replacing them with Thunder Bluff. Sunlight catches thick paint and polished horns against the soft shade of the awnings. Give one side a conspicuous receiving bench and another a quieter working seat. Highmountain craftsmanship can add branching antlers and eagle shapes to the same portable arrangement.
contexts: Painted animal faces rise above the gathering circle, their stacked bands recording clans, journeys and remembered deeds. A carver works at a fresh post beside the broad benches; chips and ochre dust gather beneath the unfinished figures. Drums, beadwork and hide awnings lend the common its own rhythm and color even among the settlement’s older walls. Guests are received where everyone can see them, while a quieter bench lets a story or disagreement unfold at greater length. A family’s place in the community can be explained through a carving here, and a public promise gains weight beneath the histories that surrounding households recognize.
hybrid: Current Shu’halo or Hi’halo culture, or applicable live Tauren heritage, provides the public custom. A hybrid can retain the story-pole gathering practice through tauren ancestry and living clan-history/civic-carving custom, including shared local motifs; Storytellers alone does not imply tauren art. Clan symbols are cultural furnishings, and sacred offerings are supplied only by an eligible faith scene.
lore: Tauren and Highmountain settlements prominently display painted carved poles; native northern stories/storytellers and communal design support oral history. A civic reading of customary art is consistent with cultural continuity when personal or county faith changes.
extrapolation: Using ordinary poles as explicit clan-history records and placing a carver and receiving bench around them is a confident civic extrapolation. Sacred ancestral communion, sun/moon doctrine and elemental effects remain with the faith catalog.

11.label: The Hideworkers’ Common
availability: Available at an existing work courtyard, market-side shelter, barn frontage or communal lodge room.
art: Rework a local shelter or barn-side courtyard as a tauren communal hidework space. Broad scraping beams and stretched leather frames line the edge, with bead trays, horn toggles, thick cord and painted panels around a large shared sewing table. Red and turquoise bands mark the sturdy wooden frames; cream hide shades leave the original roof and walls visible. Finished packs, weather cloaks and harness straps hang from a drying rail. A food pot and broad guest bench occupy the clean side, outside the raw-hide work. Contrast warm worked leather and polished bone with cool daylight from the open court. The space feels inhabited, generous and practical, with quiet pride in durable craft rather than a sacred altar or a giant industrial tannery.
contexts: Scrapers move along the stretched hides beneath a rail of finished packs and weather cloaks. Beads click into bowls as straps and horn toggles are sorted across the shared table. The clean guest bench sits beside a food pot, close enough for a visitor to discuss a fitting without entering the wet work. Families bring repairs, hunters bring materials, and a skilled maker’s judgment carries considerable weight when provisions or travel gear are being divided. Bright painted frames give the work its local identity. Conversation can run alongside the stitching, from a straightforward commission to who owes supplies before the next journey.
hybrid: Current Shu’halo/Hi’halo culture or applicable living Tauren heritage can supply the ordinary community craft venue. A hybrid may retain the tauren hidework-and-provision common from ancestry as a practical shared custom; live pastoral, hunting or leatherworking practice strengthens retention, but unrelated hunters do not automatically receive tauren furnishings. Tables and seats suit the actual resident bodies.
lore: Canon tauren leatherwork and community trade are visible in ordinary settlements; Highmountain trade includes leather goods. Native pastoralists for Shu’halo and hunters for Hi’halo support the material basis without requiring the Earth Mother religion.
extrapolation: The shared work-and-guest arrangement is a small portable institution inferred from the documented craft and communal material culture. Actual body sizes and local animals determine fittings.

11.label: The Reciprocal Trade Court
availability: Available at a settlement-edge courtyard, road-side exchange shelter or broad work landing between neighboring communities.
art: Attach a modest Highmountain trade court to the existing settlement edge or road landing. Two broad facing mats hold complementary goods: local food and leather on one side, stone samples, crafted tools or mineral colors on the other. Branching-antler and eagle carvings crown a few heavy posts, tied with thick rope beneath a practical cream hide canopy. Warm red and ochre painting repeats across baskets and bench ends. An ordinary weighing table occupies the open middle, and a sheltered bench gives two delegations equal access. Preserve the actual road, walls and landscape beyond. The arrangement should look strong, patient and deeply practical, making cooperation visible through useful goods without duplicating Thunder Totem’s gigantic architecture or its legendary hammer.
contexts: Two trading mats face each other beneath antler-carved posts. Food baskets and leather goods wait opposite samples of the neighboring community’s craft, with the weighing bench between them. Each delegation has room to display what the other lacks. Thick lashings creak above the receiving seats, and the goods smell of grain, worked hide and freshly opened stores. Agreements here are measured in useful deliveries as well as words. Visitors can inspect a disputed load, negotiate the next exchange or ask who will keep the road safe. The paired arrangement makes mutual dependence plain even when the people sharing it would prefer not to admit that dependence.

Tauren heritage alone does not export the specific Rivermane-derived institution to every Shu’halo county. Trading partners are the actual neighboring community, not automatically drogbar.

extrapolation: The form is reduced to portable paired mats and a shared weighing shelter. Replacing canonical partners and goods with the actual local neighboring communities is deliberate extrapolation; a fragile current alliance is not fabricated.

11.label: The Longrunners’ Workstead
availability: Available at an existing provision room, village-edge shelter, lodge frontage or travelers’ work yard.
art: Fit a severe, sturdy taunka workstead into the existing village shelter. Thick hide curtains, strongly braced timber, tusk-shaped entrance fittings and broad bone-handled tools create a hard-used silhouette. Longrunner packs, repaired snow or travel harnesses and rolled bedding surround raised baskets of smoke-dried food. A wide inspection table and low guest seat lie near the bright doorway, separated from the soot-dark drying rack. Deep russet, cream, cold grey and weathered bone contrast with the amber of a contained work hearth. Let the original local walls remain. In warmer lands, show lighter curtains and a ventilated drying awning while keeping the horn craft and emphatic practical arrangement. The space belongs to people who prepare thoroughly for difficult journeys.
contexts: Smoke-dried provisions hang above raised baskets while heavy packs are checked at the inspection table. A broad bone-handled awl lies beside a repaired harness, and the entrance fittings repeat the sweep of great tusks. Longrunners stop here for straps, food and news of the next stretch of road. Work is judged by whether it will survive use, and a failed fastening can earn more attention than an impressive title. Visitors have a seat near the doorway, where a commission or request for supplies can be examined piece by piece. The room’s stores make hospitality tangible, with every offered portion counted against the journeys still ahead.
hybrid: Current No’halo culture or applicable living Taunka heritage supplies the hunter/provision workstead. A hybrid can retain Taunka longrunner and hard-weather outfitting practice from ancestry; regional weather changes the materials rather than removing the practical institution. Religious elemental command is separately detected and not required.
lore: Canon Taunka settlements use northern hunting and mammoth-tusk/skull visual culture; longrunners are a documented social role. Native Hunters, Hard Working and Winter Warriors reinforce the practical identity.
extrapolation: A small shared outfit-and-provisions workstead is inferred from this material culture. Its warmer-region construction and wood-carved substitute for unavailable tusks are explicit adaptations, not new climate magic.

11.label: The Roost above the Common
availability: Available at existing roof ridges, a broad tree, a cliff shelf or supported upper platforms overlooking a settlement common. Base block requires actual winged harpy residents using upper nests. Use the accessible-hybrid variant for flightless locals retaining the cultural custom. The venue does not create offspring, captives, a named queen or a magical storm.
art: Use the settlement’s existing roof, broad tree or cliff as the base of a compact harpy roost. Ragged basket-shaped nests and crude platforms crowd the upper edge; feathers, scavenged cloth, brittle bones and polished metal scraps hang from branch lashings. A conspicuous upper seat carries the richest glittering trophies. Below it, an accessible receiving deck has a broad stair or ramp joining the ordinary common. Warm light flashes from stolen-looking trinkets while the nest interiors remain dark, crowded and unkempt. Broken baskets and gnawed scraps stain a side ledge. Preserve the old walls and landscape, emphasizing the roost’s possessive, precariously exuberant additions. If inhabitants appear in this base variant, actual harpies occupy the upper nests while visitors use the lower landing.
contexts: Ragged nests cling above the common, crowded with feathers, old cloth and gleaming scraps that flash whenever the wind moves them. Harpies trade sharp calls between the upper ledges while visitors approach the lower receiving deck. The richest collection hangs around the matron’s perch, making rank visible before anyone explains it. A sour nest smell mingles with sun-warmed rope and the dry clatter of bones. Bright gifts can win attention here, though their value may be judged by luster rather than a merchant’s scale. The landing permits bargaining, tribute or a guarded request for passage under several watchful perches at once.

Nest-shaped terraces rise above the common on broad supports, with a wide ramp leading between their rough woven edges. Feathers, bright metal scraps and old ribbons stir around the highest receiving seat. Its conspicuous trophies make the community’s favored gathering place easy to recognize among the older buildings. Sharp laughter travels between the platforms while goods and gifts are carried up from the yard. A polished trinket may start a conversation faster than a formal introduction. Visitors can bargain on the lower terrace or ascend to make a public request, watched from several levels of the same crowded, fiercely claimed common.
hybrid: Current Harpy culture or applicable avianic heritage can supply the roost-and-trophy custom. Harpy ancestry may preserve the same nest-shaped terraces and collecting practice in a hybrid. The base block is for a resident winged community with ground-accessible public reception; select the complete accessible-hybrid variant when flightless locals retain the custom. A culture change does not give converts wings, eggs or talons.
lore: Warcraft documents harsh matriarchal competition, foul raised nests, glittering-object collection and trading/protection relationships with other peoples. GoA2’s live Harpy culture includes hills, hunters, adaptive skirmishing and female martial leadership.
extrapolation: Roosts attached to existing roofs and a ground-accessible receiving deck extrapolate a migrating harpy settlement feature. Every visitor is not automatically attacked or captured; the scene preserves the institution’s menace and social possibilities.

11.label: The Honey-and-Herb Den
availability: Available at a local cellar, earthen room, woodland shelter or existing household/work building with a sheltered visitor threshold.
art: Adapt an existing cellar, low workroom or bank-side shelter into a furbolg honey-and-herb den. Thick wooden shelves hold sealed honey crocks, bundles of dried leaves, bark containers and squat brewing vats. A broad tasting bench stands near the entrance, with heavy cups, woven baskets and beaded animal-shaped craft. Warm amber vessel colors glow against deep brown timber, dark green herbs and softened hide partitions. The original local stone, plaster or roots remain visible. A partly opened vat and hanging herb rack make the room a working place, not a shrine. Give the entrance a clear gift-setting surface and keep family stores farther inside. Show patient handmade practicality and weighty rounded forms; living bears, magical corruption and twin-god statues are unnecessary.
contexts: Honey and dried leaves scent the den’s sheltered entrance. Stout cups stand beside sealed crocks, while a brew vat occupies the warmer recess behind the tasting bench. Bundled herbs and beaded clan craft hang from heavy shelves. Guests set a gift or useful ingredient at the threshold before entering the working space; a shared taste can give unfamiliar words something practical to refer to. Recipes, remedies and the value of a gathered plant can be discussed close to the stores. The deeper household recess stays quiet, making the front bench a place where guarded acquaintance may grow into a useful exchange.
hybrid: Current Furbolg culture or living jalgaric heritage supplies the practical den. A hybrid may retain furbolg honeybrewing or herbcraft through ancestry and a continuing household craft, including local ingredients and a shared dwarf-style brew; unrelated Medicinal Plants or Brewery alone does not assign furbolg art. Furnishings fit actual bodies rather than turning cultural converts into bears.
lore: Canon furbolg honey tending, brewing and clan craft combine with GoA2 Medicinal Plants and isolationist ethos. The Local Flavors quest directly supports a dwarf/furbolg mixed brewing practice rather than making hybrids merely a theoretical possibility.
extrapolation: Combining these crafts into a portable receiving work-den, and using ingredient gifts as a practical opening, is a scene extrapolation. It does not prescribe every furbolg host’s generosity or refusal; bear-god teaching belongs to eligible faith venues.

11.label: The Pack’s Plunder Yard
availability: Available at a settlement-edge camp, neglected courtyard, broken shed frontage or defensible roadside clearing.
art: Turn an existing rough yard or roadside clearing into a gnoll pack common without replacing the surrounding settlement. Bone-braced hide awnings lean above a jumble of cracked shields, bent pans, battered armor and stripped wagon fittings. Trophy stakes and crude tooth-shaped marks claim the perimeter; a greasy cooking rack occupies the smoky edge. A worn dirt patch remains clear beside a raised seat assembled from the largest spoils. Use dirty tan, rust-red, dark hide and chalky bone with rough lashings and exaggerated jagged silhouettes. Show gnawed refuse and heavy scavenged craft rather than an orderly merchants’ market. Visitors approach an obvious front bench where their goods can be watched from the surrounding shelters. No decay spell or universal humanoid-skin tent is necessary.
contexts: Bent shields, pans and wagon fittings crowd the pack’s yard beneath bone-braced awnings. Meat smoke hangs over the cooking rack, and trophies rattle on the boundary stakes. Arguments about useful spoils carry across the bare challenge ground, where an impressive display can draw more attention than a careful explanation. The largest heap supports the pack’s conspicuous receiving seat. Visitors bring something the watchers can recognize as food, equipment or advantage, and bargaining takes place within view of several shelters. The shared ground gives a chief’s order room to carry, but it also gives rivals, offended claimants and unsuccessful hunters an audience.
hybrid: Current Gnoll culture or applicable live hyenaic heritage supplies the rough pack common. A hybrid can retain gnoll ancestry’s plunder-sharing, challenge-yard or warband-salvage custom when it remains part of local practice. GoA2 Might Is Right/Battlefield Looters reinforce retention but unrelated looter cultures do not automatically become gnoll camps. Actual residents retain their own physiology.
lore: Canon gnoll camps, raids and trophies supply the material context; native Warrior Culture, Might Is Right, Quarrelsome and Battlefield Looters directly support dominance and plunder as cultural emphases. The game’s crafted gnoll tent confirms bone-and-hide materials.
extrapolation: A single clear challenge-and-receiving patch inside a salvage common is inferred scene organization. It retains the archetype without turning an RPG-only exhaustive social hierarchy into asserted Warcraft canon.

11.label: The Hunt-and-Horn Yard
availability: Available at a village common, hunting camp, low work shelter or existing yard beside household stores.
art: Overlay an existing hunting yard or low shelter with wolvar material life. Stretched hides hang from thick stakes around a smoky provision corner. A broad horn-carving block holds chips, awls and unfinished trinkets; curved trophies jut from the nearest shelter roof. Add a compact sturdy chicken pen, a rough gift table and densely knotted territorial markers. Earthy russet, cream fur, dark wood and polished horn contrast with whatever woodland, snow or grass lies locally beyond. Keep the huts and work pieces squat and substantial without forcing every resident to be a wolvar. The clear central patch connects visitors, the food store and the hunters’ return route. Show a brisk working camp with an unmistakably possessive silhouette, not an altar to a named yeti.
contexts: Horn chips lie beneath the carving block beside a rack of heavy hides. The food store smells of smoke, and an impatient clucking comes from the pen at its edge. Hunters display their returns where the whole common can inspect them, with trophies above the receiving table and tools close at hand. A visitor’s useful gift earns a practical examination before a longer conversation begins. The crowded ground can host a boast, a complaint about a hunt or an offer of help against a troublesome beast. Its marked boundaries make belonging conspicuous, while the table leaves room for outsiders who have something worth discussing.
hybrid: Current Wolvar culture or applicable living lupine heritage supplies the hunt-yard custom. A hybrid can retain wolvar trophy work, food-husbandry and warband gathering through ancestry and a continuing hunting/common practice; generic Sacred Hunts alone does not establish wolvar styling. Seating and access fit the actual residents.
lore: Game pet-journal text documents wolvar horn-carving; Flown the Coop! documents the chicken house and everyday food concerns. Canon wolvar can form diplomatic relationships despite a territorial reputation, and native Sacred Hunts/Tribe Unity support the communal hunting frame.
extrapolation: Combining these ordinary practices into a migrating hunt-and-craft yard is a modest inference. Local horn and prey replace Sholazar-specific animals; Kartak, shoveltusk shrines, proto-dragons and robot worship remain faith/location dependent.

11.label: The Thornbound Warband Yard
availability: Available at an existing enclosure, rough village court, scrub-edge common or defensible camp clearing.
art: Keep the local court or clearing visible behind an emphatically quilboar enclosure. Hooked branches and tall thorn stakes are woven into spiky screens, with tusk-shaped posts framing a narrow, watched entrance. Boar-marked shields, hide mats, rough clay jars and cord-tied tools gather around a low supply table. Freshly bound brush and a small tended bramble strip show the stockade’s maintenance. Use reddish earth, dark brown wood, pale tusk forms and dusty hide under strong warm light. The settlement’s existing building remains behind the overlay, so the yard does not become a new Razorfen. Compose a broad inner work patch beneath a jagged perimeter, with a sheltered receiving seat and room to inspect stores or lay out a weapon.
contexts: Hooked thorn screens enclose the warband’s common around a rough supply table. Tusk-shaped gateposts narrow the approach, while boar-marked shields and tied bundles of replacement brush line the inner fence. Dry leaves scrape the woven edges whenever the wind rises. Visitors enter where the watchers can see their hands and their goods. A dispute over grazing, stolen stores or passage can be argued beside the same table where supplies are divided. Fresh lashings show how much labor goes into keeping the boundary sound. Inside the bristling perimeter, family loyalty and a warband’s territorial claims have a very tangible shape.
hybrid: Current Quilboar culture or applicable agamagganic heritage supplies the thorn-enclosed warband custom. A hybrid can retain quilboar fortification/craft and territorial gathering practice through ancestry; thorn silhouettes and boar emblems can be inherited without adopting the ancestral faith or growing quills. Warriors of the Dry alone does not establish this culture.
lore: Canon quilboar settlements favor thorn-defined territories and deploy transported bramble pods through thornweaving. Native Tribe Unity, Quarrelsome and martial customs support a warband common independently of divine blood ritual.
extrapolation: A modest maintained thorn stockade using ordinary local brush is the portable extrapolation. Immense Razorfen growth, blood-fed spellwork, sacred Agamaggan remains and boar-god offerings are not automatic culture furnishings.

11.label: The Coiled Shade Court

art: Overlay an existing court with a modest sethrak craft shelter. Curved low display platforms leave generous paths around them, while portable cobra-hood screens and carved serpentine corner fittings frame the shaded working edge. Woven turquoise cloth, ochre leather, restrained gold-metal detail and scaled geometric borders supply the unmistakable design. Covered water jars and a small wash basin stand beside trays of finished fittings, tools and neatly folded material. Preserve the settlement’s original wall rather than painting a temple across the whole district. Bright regional daylight falls across the clear court while the working seats remain cool and sheltered. Give visitors a broad examination table and a visible receiving position; the striking silhouettes should feel refined, orderly and inhabited.

Turquoise cloth hangs from hood-shaped screens, and scaled borders repeat across fittings, folded material and covered water jars. Craftspeople display finished pieces where a visitor can inspect them without stepping into the tools. The broad receiving space accommodates an escort or a bulky load, while the quieter seats under the canopy suit a longer negotiation. Work is presented with visible care: an uneven edge or mismatched pattern stands out against the ordered display. A commission, a disputed delivery or a request for assistance can be considered here among the community’s ordinary practical wares.

11.label: The Shellwrights’ Yard
availability: Available at an existing small work yard, shelter frontage, market-side bench or mercenary outfitting corner. Supply can be ordinary local/traded shell pieces or a modest retained stock. Giant-shell buildings and turtle riding require actual large-shell/animal availability and are not selected from culture alone.
art: Add an Oomlot shell-working corner to the existing yard rather than replacing the local houses. Rounded shell sections, sturdy shell helmets and small ridged vessels lie beside lashing cord, awls and a half-woven mat. A portable awning repeats overlapping scute shapes above the original short benches; one ordinary-height visitor surface provides clear room to inspect goods. Warm ochre, dark shell brown, rough reed and sunlit polished ridges define the palette. Local walls and regional plants remain behind the work. Show small, ingenious use of strong natural materials, with repaired cracks and neatly fitted straps giving objects weight. No gigantic shell roof, summoned turtle, sacrificial fire or racial caricature is needed for the recognizable material signature.
contexts: Shell ridges catch the light above a yard full of fitted straps, woven mats and rounded helmets. Awls and binding cord lie beside a carefully repaired crack, while finished pieces wait on the visitor’s inspection surface. The shelter’s overlapping roof shapes echo the same strong material at a smaller scale. Workers can discuss a commission by trying a fastening, comparing a shell’s thickness or showing where a repair will hold. Travelers and hired fighters bring battered equipment to the bench; local households bring vessels and shelter fittings. The clear patch beside the tools gives an outsider room to bargain without crowding the compact working stations.
hybrid: Current Oomlot culture or applicable living pygmy heritage supports this material craft. A hybrid can retain Oomlot shellwork, fitted helmet craft or ridged portable shelter furnishings through ancestry; actual body sizes determine bench and helmet scale. The practice does not require pygmy anatomy, Volcanoth worship or giant island turtles.
lore: Canon pygmy equipment and ordinary architecture use turtle shells; native Oomlot Swords for Hire and Hit and Run support a useful outfitting application. The craft survives independently of the Volcanoth religious storyline.
extrapolation: A portable shellwright’s work corner and shell-ridge awning generalize documented material use. Traded shell stock, local substitutes and resized visitor access make migration plausible without inventing giant turtles or a universal shell-built city.

11.label: The Murloc Catch Commons
availability: Available at a waterside settlement, fishing landing or market with a local catch supply. A fishery or reliable transported catch supply; no underwater breathing is required for the default scene.
art: Create a painterly Warcraft scene in a wide 16:9 view of a busy fishing edge. The original local quay or riverbank remains visible beneath a disorderly cluster of small peaked huts, muddy reed screens and timber drying frames. Wet silver catches cover woven mats; bone hooks, forked spears and nets weighted with mismatched shells lean against the poles. Smoke curls from a low cooking pit, gulls wheel above and shallow water reflects bright scraps of rope and scale. The composition opens toward a clear visitor landing while the tangled work area fills one side. Convey exuberant, noisy, improvised tribal industry through rough materials and dense little details, without replacing the settlement with a famous murloc village.
contexts: Fish scales sparkle across the sorting mats, and the air smells of smoke, brine and yesterday’s catch. Nets slap the poles while sharp calls and bubbling answers pass between the workers. A good haul brings trading, boasting and arguments over which basket belongs to which fishing party; a lean one turns the same shared space into a reckoning of debts. Visitors wait at the landing rather than walking across the wet nets. Fresh food, a borrowed boat, news from another shore or an accusation of stolen fishing grounds can all find an audience here.
hybrid: Use the live county culture, not the ruler or resident race. A hybrid with native murloc ancestry may retain this ordinary community practice and its portable styling; no separate institution flag is required for the modest venue. An unrelated culture needs deliberate adoption of this catalog practice. Use the accessible adaptation for the actual local residents. Keep the clattering communal fish work and peaked reed accents; widen passages and work heights for the actual inhabitants.

extrapolation: A modest communal catch-sorting area is a portable extension of the fishing village, with visitor etiquette authored for RP.

11.label: The Gorloc Bug-Pot Shelter
availability: Available at an ordinary shaded cooking shelter or open-sided village gathering place near usable water.
art: Paint a warm, slightly chaotic Warcraft cooking shelter in a wide 16:9 composition. A raised timber platform fits into the existing village edge, shaded by overlapping broad leaves lashed over an open frame. Shallow baskets hold edible beetles and grubs, fish hang beneath the eaves, and a bubbling pot sends spicy steam through the green-gold light. Small gourds, mismatched bowls and bundled seasoning crowd a practical preparation bench. Low comfortable perches curve around the meal area, with broader visitor steps at the front. Beyond the canopy, preserve the local buildings and vegetation. The visual character is earthy, affectionate, curious and pungent: everyday gorloc domestic life, with no sacred shiny pile or Titan mechanism at its center.
contexts: A peppery steam drifts through the leaf roof, carrying the unmistakable smell of fish and roasted insects. Cooked bugs are offered with the same enthusiasm as a new story, while empty bowls become props in increasingly elaborate accounts of the day’s adventures. The raised shelter catches every breeze; its comfortable perches make leaving harder than arriving. A visitor can share food, offer a strange ingredient, ask after a missing traveler or endure a cheerful argument about what counts as delicious. Gifts meant for supper are passed to the cook; promises and gossip circulate much farther than the smoke.
hybrid: Use the live county culture, not the ruler or resident race. A hybrid with native gorloc ancestry may retain this ordinary community practice and its portable styling; no separate institution flag is required for the modest venue. An unrelated culture needs deliberate adoption of this catalog practice. Use the accessible adaptation for the actual local residents. Provide broad steps and seats of mixed height; food suitable for other bodies can share the hearth without erasing the gorloc dishes.
lore: Gorloc leaf-thatched raised houses and bug/fish diet are documented. Native Esteemed Hospitality and storytellers support the public use.
extrapolation: An informal shared cooking shelter; no universal Oracle allegiance, shrine or Sholazar intelligence effect.

availability: Available at a fishing landing, riverside shed or workshop supplying a local fishery. A local fishing community or landing supplying fishery work.
art: Show an active net-mending commons in a wide painterly Warcraft frame. The existing quay shed or riverside awning is adapted with curved bone braces, amber hide wind screens and blue-green painted storage boxes. A great net hangs loosely across two beams, its broken meshes marked by small ties. Bone needles, rope, carved floats and harpoon fittings cover shared benches; a partially repaired boat fitting rests near a tub of clean water. A visitor can ask for passage, buy a harpoon fitting, learn which water is dangerous or bring a damaged net as proof of trouble.
